2. Hot/Cold Weather Emergencies

1.3. These operations will automatically go into effect upon a declaration of such an Emergency by the Mayor. These operations shall also be put into effect whenever, in the opinion of the Fire Chief, or the designated alternate, such action would be beneficial to the effective utilization of available personnel and equipment during periods of unusual and/or prolonged temperature extremes.
1.4. In a declared Emergency, the Division of Fire will work closely with City and County Health Departments, Franklin County EMA, and the Division of Police.
1.5. As determined by the exact nature of the Emergency, the Fire Chief may initiate all, or any combination of, the following actions:
1.5.1. Building inspections, hydrant work, and all outside training will be suspended.
2.1.1. All “instant” vacation will be denied.
1.5.2. All fire stations will becomedrop-off sites for publicly donated heating/cooling devices.

1.5.3. Fire stations will serve as distribution points for heating/cooling devices; however, prioritization of delivery or distribution will be the responsibility of a social service organization such as the City Health Department or the Red Cross.
1.5.4. During the emergency, and continuing for as long as determined by the Fire Chief, Fire Prevention personnel may be temporarily reassigned in other areas on a day-by-day basis.
1.5.5. House Captains will each develop a list of potentially vulnerable residents in their “first in” areas. Visitations will then be made by the companies to check on these residents.
1.5.6. During cold emergencies, public education will be focused on fire prevention and specifically safe heating practices.
1.5.7. During a heat emergency, the Fire Division will assist in opening and closing hydrants as part of “Operation Cool Down.”

1.5.8. During heat emergencies, public education will be focused on first aid and prevention of heat related illness. When appropriate to the emergency, public education will also address water conservation.
Section 1 Administration

1.1 Purpose: The purpose of this procedure is to describe the roles and responsibilities of a Fire Chaplain and the Fire Chaplain Team, also referred to in this and other SOPs as “Chaplain(s)”, “Fire Chaplain(s)”, and “Division Chaplain(s)”. Additional procedures and guidelines shall be provided by the Members Support Unit Supervisor.

1.2 Responsibility: It shall be the responsibility of each member to know, understand and utilize these procedures as they apply to the situation at hand. It shall further be the responsibility of all Division Officers to train their subordinates in the proper application of these procedures and to implement and enforce the use of these procedures.
Section 2 General – Role of the Fire Chaplain
2.1 Fire Chaplains serve the Columbus Division of Fire by providing support, encouragement and hope to Division of Fire members, retirees, and their families.

2.2 Fire Chaplains assist Division of Fire members in developing and maintaining overall wellness, building individual, crew and station readiness in strengthening spirit, moral character and mental resilience and endurance by providing pastoral care and counsel.

2.3 The Fire Chaplain Team functions as part of the Members Support Unit, emphasizing the spiritual wellbeing of the members of the Columbus Division of Fire. The central aspects of spirituality are attributed to meaning, purpose and connectedness, expressed through beliefs, values, traditions and practices.
Section 3 Chaplain Duties

3.1 Fire Chaplains’ primary duty will be to provide a ministry of presence in order to provide compassionate and empathetic support during ceremonial events, crisis situations, and on a day-to-day basis. Fire Chaplain services shall include:
3.1.1 Support and provide assistance to members of the Division of Fire and their families in times of illness and bereavement, and for their spiritual wellbeing.
3.1.2 Visit sick or injured Division of Fire members in homes and hospitals, upon request.
3.1.3 Attend and participate, upon request, in funerals for active and retired Division of Fire members, as available.
3.1.4 Offer prayers, invocations and benedictions at official Division of Fire ceremonies such as graduations, promotions, award ceremonies, award dinners, building and apparatus dedications, etc.
3.1.5 Respond to other situations when the need of a Fire Chaplain is apparent or is requested.
3.1.6 Function as a member of the Peer Support Team, per SOP 04-03-03, as long as they remain on the Fire Chaplain Team.
3.1.7 Upon request, function as a Family Support Liaison for family crisis notification, per SOP 04-03-01 and 04-03-02.
Section 4 Procedures

4.1 When a Division of Fire member determines that they have a personal need for the services of the Fire Chaplain, they may either contact the Fire Chaplain directly, a member of the Peer Support Team or the Members Support Office.
4.2 When there is an urgent request or when a perceived need for a Fire Chaplain occurs during the evening, on a weekend or holiday, contact ES2.
4.3 An up-to-date list of all current members of the Fire Chaplain Team will be maintained. This list shall contain all information necessary to make contact with the Fire Chaplains.
4.4 Firefighters interested in applying for a Division of a Fire Chaplain position shall be directed to the Division of Fire, Members Support Unit Supervisor.
4.5 Firefighters interested in becoming a Fire Chaplain shall submit a resume to the Members Support Unit Supervisor, etc. See Section 7 for minimal qualifications.
Section 5 Confidentiality

5.1 Communications with Fire Chaplains are classified as privileged communications under Ohio Revised Code Section 2317.02 (C) as a cleric and 2317.02 (K) as a CISM team member, and thereby protected as confidential.

5.2 Fire Chaplains shall keep conversations with Division of Fire personnel in absolute confidence and shall not release information to the news media, insurance agencies, or attorneys regarding cases in which they are involved or have knowledge of. The only justified breach of confidentiality is if there is a threat or perceived threat to the safety of the member receiving counsel, the Fire Chaplain or others.

5.3 Fire Chaplains shall take all means necessary to protect the setting of confidential communications, including within Division of Fire facilities, so as not to be heard or read, intentionally or unintentionally, by other Division of Fire members. This protection shall include verbal and written communications, including text messages, social media, etc.
Section 6 Expectations for Chaplains
6.1 Show an active interest in chaplaincy and be willing and able to perform those duties.
6.2 Maintain ethical and moral standards consistent with the City of Columbus Central Work Rules, the chaplaincy credentialing agency, and the religion or denomination that endorsed the candidate.
6.3 Have an awareness and competency to address the diverse cultural and religious preferences of Division of Fire members.

6.4 Have a readiness, without proselytizing, to answer questions and participate in discussions initiated by Division of Fire member, a Division of Fire member’s family, a retiree, or citizen of Columbus.
6.1 Become and remain a member of the Peer Support Team.
6.2 Be reasonably available to all Division of Fire members, upon request.
Section 7 Qualifications

7.1 All interested candidates for the Fire Chaplain Team must have completed the apprenticeship program, obtained journeyman status, and be in good standing with the Division of Fire and with their local congregation.
7.1 All candidates desiring to serve as Fire Chaplains shall:

7.1.1 Be ordained or licensed in one of the recognized religions or denominations, with five years of experience, or willing to be trained through the chaplaincy credentialing agency approved by the Division of Fire. Fire Chaplain responsibilities may vary according to levels of experience.

7.1.2 Submit an RT-154 and resume submitted through the proper chain of command to the Members Support Supervisor. The RT-154 and resume shall include relevant information regarding the candidate’s desires, passions, skills, abilities, and qualifications to be considered a Fire Chaplain.
7.1.3 Submit three letters of recommendation which must include: a letter from an ordained religious leader, a member of the candidate’s congregation, and a member of the Division of Fire.
7.1.4 Participate in the Fire Chaplain Selection Committee interview process.
7.2 Questions and concerns should be directed to the Fire Chaplain Coordinator in the Members Support office.
Section 8 Identification and Uniform Guidelines

8.1 Fire Chaplains will be issued a Division of Fire ID badge which will include a banner at the bottom with the designation "Chaplain". Fire Chaplains will be required to exchange their current Division of Fire ID badge at the time of receipt of their Fire Chaplain ID badge. Additionally, any chaplains removed from the team will exchange their Fire Chaplain ID badge for a standard Division of Fire ID badge.
8.2 Fire Chaplains participating in official Division of Fire ceremonies shall wear their Class A uniform.

8.3 Fire Chaplains will be issued a Chaplain bar to be attached to their Division Class A uniform according to approved uniform guidelines. Any chaplains who are removed from the team or placed on an inactive status will return the chaplain bar to the Chaplain Coordinator in the Members Support Office.
8.4 Fire Chaplains responding while on duty for request for a station, hospital or home visitation shall wear their fatigue uniform.

8.5 Fire Chaplains responding for visitations while off duty, shall wear approved attire with the identifying Chaplain or Peer Support Team logos and be dressed in a manner that represents the professional standards of the Fire Chaplain Team.
Section 9 Chaplain Training
9.1 Newly appointed Fire Chaplains are required to complete a Basic Chaplain Training Course provided by the chaplaincy credentialing agency approved by the Division of Fire.

9.2 Continuing education for Fire Chaplains will be provided on a regular basis to strengthen and empower the Fire Chaplain Team to provide high-quality service, improve effectiveness, align efforts, share best practices, and mature the professionalism of Fire Chaplains for the benefit of the Division of Fire.
9.3 Fire Chaplains are expected to attend training opportunities that are provided by the Members Support Office and approved by the Fire Chief.
9.4 All required chaplaincy membership, training, licensure and certification requirements shall be paid for by the Division of Fire.
Section 10 Change in Membership Status
10.1 Fire Chaplain membership is revocable at any time at the discretion of the Members Support Office. Revocation may occur for, but is not limited to, the following:
10.1.1 Any violation, misrepresentation or inability to fulfill the expectations for Fire Chaplains, as listed in Section 6.

10.1.2 Any violation, or perceived violation, of confidentiality, as listed in Section 5. A perceived violation can be considered to be as damaging to the effectiveness of the Fire Chaplain Team and Peer Support Team as any true violation of confidentiality.
10.1.1 Any misrepresentation of the Chaplain Team or its function.
10.1.3 Continued absenteeism or lack of participation at Chaplain meetings or training sessions or activities.
10.1.2 Acting against the express direction of the Members Support Office.

10.1.4 At the discretion of the Members Support Office for any violation, discipline investigation, or complaint against Peer member when discovered during annual audit with the Administrative Chiefs office.
10.2 Chaplains wishing to resign or go inactive for a designated period from the Team shall submit a letter of intention to the Members Support Office Supervisor.

10.2.1 Resigning from the Chaplain team: Volunteering to give up membership and certification would require the member to go back through the application process, training process, and complete the Basic Chaplain Training Course as described in Section 7 and
Section 9 if they ever chose to join the team again.

10.2.2 Inactive status from Chaplain team: Asking to be temporarily not utilized on the Chaplain Team for a variety of reasons. Examples: Death in family, divorce, change in life circumstances, etc. This is not to be used punitively but encouraged to maintain a good work life balance and to stay in a positive and healthy state of mind.

10.2 If a Chaplain chooses to or it is suggested that Chaplain should move to inactive status, the Members Support Supervisor and member(s) of the Chaplain team shall continue to support the Chaplain and follow up regularly during period of being inactive. Inactivation and reactivation of any Chaplain will be determined by the Members Support Supervisor.
10.3 A Chaplain that is placed on inactive status on the Peer Support Team will automatically be placed on inactive status on the Chaplain Team.
10.1.3 If a Chaplain is removed from the Peer Support Team, they will automatically be removed from the Chaplain Team.

1. DEFINITIONS:

3.1 LODD: Line of Duty Death. The death of an active member resulting from injury while responding to or actively participating at an Emergency scene OR the death of an active member resulting from an illness or disease that is directly contributable to on duty exposure. (i.e.. Presumptive Cancer, COVID, etc.). The member might be retired just prior to passing for benefit purposes to their family.
3.1 Active Member: A fire division member serving in an active capacity who passes away as a result of a non-job-related accident.
3.2 InactiveMember: A retired or former member in good standing of the division.
3.3 Affiliate Member: An individual such as division Chaplain, Box 15 member, or Auxiliary member.
3.4 Non-Job-Related Death: A death that is not Fire or EMS duty related. This could be from accidental or intentional causes. See the chart for further classification.

3. FUNERAL HONOR GUARD SERVICES: The family must be consulted and agree to the department’s participation in providing funeral Honor Guard Services. Throughout the entire funeral process, the family’s wishes shall be considered and followed with the understanding that family may choose to forgo an appropriate Honor Guard Service; but at no time shall Classifications violate section 5.

4.1 Viewing Detail: A detail of two Honor Guards posted at the casket at all times during viewing hours. This is accomplished with a minimum of four members for each set of viewing hours. If the viewing is in excess of two hours, add two additional Honor Guard members to the detail.

4.2 Rifle Detail: An Honor Guard contingent of up to seven riflemen and one officer in charge (OIC) for presentation of a three-shot volley. This is for a LODD, or if the member is an active or honorably discharged military member.

4.3 Flag Fold: The American flag may be draped on the casket for any LODD or if the deceased was honorably discharged or active in the United States Armed Forces. The American flag is provided by the funeral director, through the Veterans Administration. A subordinate flag may be used to drape the casket if the deceased was not a veteran. At the time of internment, an American flag (if a LODD or veteran) or the CFD approved Remembrance flag can be folded and presented to the family. CFD Remembrance flags are provided by the Honor Guard and purchased by the Local 67 Charity Foundation. Columbus Division of Fire: Funeral Procedures S.O.P. 09-04-25 3 of 5
4.1 Bugler: A person to play taps.

4.4 Station Drive By: The funeral procession will drive by a fire station with apparatus on front ramp and the assigned members at attention. It is customary to present a hand salute during the passing of the hearse and family car only
4.2 Uniform Turn Out: Division personnel in attendance to wear class “A” uniform.

4.5 Raised Aerials: Two raised aerial ladders along the funeral procession route or at the cemetery entrance. The American flag may be hung from the apex with the star union (blue field) oriented North or East.
4.6 Color Guard: An Honor Guard unit carrying the national and subordinate flag(s). This will consist of one OIC, two guards, an American flagman and a member for each subordinate flag.

4.7 Honorary Pallbearers: Uniformed members not assigned to carry the casket. These pallbearers are placed in an honorary position leading the casket, with the family selected pallbearers actually carrying the casket.
4.3 Active Pallbearers: Uniform members assigned to actually carry the casket.

4.8 Flag at Half-Staff: National flag flown at half-staff at all Columbus Fire Stations with approval of the Mayor. The flags are to be returned to full-staff as prompted by an announcement from the FAO or preceding the internment at sundown. The national flag flown at half-staff shall not have a subordinate flag on staff
4.9 Shrouds: A ½” to 3/4” piece of black material over a divisional badge or logo.

4.9.1 Badge Shrouds: Black Badge Shrouds over the divisional badge horizontally. This is a reflection of mourning and is reserved only for Classification 1 funerals. Badge shrouds should only be worn by the department of the deceased member.
4.9.2 Logo Shroud: On any division logo (Vehicle, apparatus, sign) diagonal top left to bottom right if used.
4.10 Divisional Hearse: A fire department vehicle to carry the casket. The vehicle is usually from the company or station of the deceased.
4.11 Bagpiper / Pipes and Drum band: Piperto play music and used in the traditional fire service ceremony. The entire Pipes and Drum band may be requested for a Classification 1 or 2 funeral.
4.12 Honor Detail: Division uniform turnout and visiting department’s members present to pay tribute. This includes a Uniform procession past the casket/ urn at the end of the service.
4.13 Last Alarm: An alarm or announcement broadcast over the divisional PA and/or radio, usually at the internment site during the ceremony.
4.14 Processional Apparatus: Division apparatus included in the funeral procession but not used as a hearse.
4.15 Bell Service: A bell rung as a symbol of respect to a deceased firefighter to signal their last alarm. The code of 3-3-3 is the traditional signal of “companies have returned to quarters”.

4.16 Station Bunting: Funeral bunting or morning drapes that are placed on the outside of the deceased’s assigned station. This includes the CFD Mourning Flag to be flown on the flag pole at the deceased members assigned Station. Columbus Division of Fire: Funeral Procedures S.O.P. 09-04-25 4 of 5

1. Administration
1.1. Purpose: To describe the procedure for personnel that are separating from service with the Division of Fire.

1.2. Responsibility: It shall be the responsibility of each member to know, understand and utilize these procedures as they apply to the situation at hand. It shall further be the responsibility of all Division Officers to train their subordinates in the proper application of these procedures and to implement and enforce the use of these procedures.
1. Types of Separation

1.3. Personnel that wish to separate in “Good Standing” whether through resignation or retirement, shall make notice to the Fire Chief and/or his/her designee two weeks prior of the anticipated separation date to be considered in “Good Standing” with the Division.
1.4. Personnel that are terminated or resign in lieu of termination are considered to be in “Not Good Standing” with the Division.
2. Procedure

2.1. For an employee to separate from the Division of Fire in “Good Standing”, Human Resources must receive a time stamped written notice no less than two weeks prior to the date of separation. A Division email will be accepted as notification when sent to the Human Resource Manager and must be sent from the employee designated division email as a signature and time stamp.

2.2. Personnel wishing to receive farewell comments from the Division may submit a secondary letter through their Chain of Command with their intent to retire or resign. This letter will be placed within their permanent personnel file and can be requested at any time. NOTE – This submission through the Chain of Command does not override the two-week commitment for notice to Human Resources.

2.3. Uniformed personnel must return select Division issued items by completing a PI-31, set a time to meet with Support Services for return of property and provide a signature receipt. A notification of the returned property will also be made to Payroll.
2.4. Per the collective bargaining agreement, uniformed personnel that wish to retain their badge, helmet and Class A uniform must submit a written request to the Fire Chief.

2.5. Uniformed personnel may also request to retain their weapon, if received from the Division while working in the Bomb Squad or Fire Investigations areas, by submitting a written request to the Fire Chief.

2.6. Uniformed personnel classified as “Not Good Standing” shall complete PI-31e and return all items identified and set a time with Support Services for return of issued items and provide a signature.
3. Rights
3.1. The Fire Chief reserves the right to approve or deny the badge, helmet, Class A uniform and/or retirement identification card, if requested.
3.2. The Public Safety Director reserves the right to determine the standing of an employee with the City of Columbus after separation from the Division of Fire.
1. Administration

1.1. Purpose: Allow E-Step Firefighters with Paramedic Certification, who were allowed to downgrade their status with the Division, will have the ability to optin for selected period(s) throughout the year in order to utilize their certification.

1.2. Responsibility: It shall be the responsibility of each member to know, understand and utilize these procedures as they apply to the situation at hand. It shall further be the responsibility of all Division Officers to train their subordinates in the proper application of these procedures and to implement and enforce the use of these procedures.

1.3. Conflict: This SOP shall not be construed as invalidating, preempting, or superseding any previously issued operating procedure, rule and/or protocol. Conflicts with other SOPs, rules, and/or protocols shall be brought to the immediate attention of the member’s supervisor so that it can be evaluated by the Fire Chief, or designee, and adjusted if necessary.
2. Information

1.4. Every year the Division of Fire gives its personnel an opportunity to downgrade their Paramedic status with the Division. The downgrade is spelled out in the collective bargaining agreement between Local 67 IAFF and the City of Columbus 12.2(C). This opportunity does not require the member to downgrade their certification with the State of Ohio. The downgrade status makes them unavailable for use in a Paramedic position.

1.5. Those members granted downgrade status still have the opportunity to keep their certification with Division for training and education. The members must attend the scheduled training days that all Paramedics attend.

1.6. Those members that have maintained their Paramedic status while in Paramedic downgradestatus can choose to opt-in on a limited basis based on the needs of the Division as determined by the Fire Chief.
3. Implementation
1.7. Members can opt-in for a minimum of one transfer cycle. The Fire Chief, based on current needs of the Division, will determine the number of members granted opt-in status.
1.8. The Fire Chief reserves the right to determine the needs of the opt-in program and may limit the number of personnel granted or remaining in the program.

1.9. Those members who have a current certification and have been in downgrade status for a year or less will not be required to go through a retraining period. Those members that have a current certification and have been in downgrade status for longer than a year will be evaluated by the Training Bureau and/or EMS Officers to determine any training needs prior to being added to the authorized list.

1.10. Members wishing to opt-in shall submit a request (ES-221 EMS Opt-in Application) through the chain-of-command to the Fire Chief. The effective date of the opt-in will be once evaluated by the Training Bureau and/orEMS Officers, ALL training needs are met, and the opt-in checklist has been completely signed-off (See 3.3).

1.11. Members who opt-in will be paid the Paramedic Differential, Transport Stipend, and I/C Stipend according to the provisions of the Collective Bargaining Agreement upon being added to the authorized list.
1.12. Members who opt-in will be scheduled into the next series of CE classes given by the Division, if not current with the State of Ohio’s three-year renewal cycle.

1.13. Members opting in shall be considered in the pool of usable Paramedics until such time they notify the Fire Chief in writing their desire to opt-out, or until notified by the Division that their opt-in status is discontinued.

1.14. Members wishing to opt-out shall submit a request (RT-154) through the chain-of-command to the Fire Chief by the expiration of the Vacancy list. The effective date of the opt-out will be the effective date of the subsequent transfer list.
4. Additional

1.15. Members wishing to bid on a position with a Paramedic qualification MUST complete requirements outlined above in 3.3 and 3.4 PRIOR to the expiration of the relevant vacancy list. It will be the member’s sole responsibility to ensure that they meet all requirements. Failure to meet the opt-in requirements PRIOR to the expiration of the relevant vacancy list will cause member to be ineligible for consideration to that position regardless of seniority or starting the process outlined above in 3.3 or 3.4.

1.16. Members, who opt-in for purposes of obtaining a Paramedic qualified position, will be added to the authorized list and will be required to maintain their Paramedic qualification until authorized to drop per 12.2(C) of the Collective Bargaining Contract.

1.17. While in the Paramedic opt-in status, the member will be eligible to work Paramedic overtime and special duty as long as the member is proficient in any venue specific specialty training in accordance with current operating procedures.
1.18. The member will be afforded the same overtime privileges as any other Paramedic with the Division.

1.19. Members electing to opt-in will have their overtime hours adjusted to the average overtime hours of current Paramedics on their unit. Once the opt-in period is completed, members not renewing their opt-in status will have their overtime hours adjusted back to reflect actualovertime hours worked for the year.

1.20. Unless a petition for change has been granted, a member’s assignment and Kelly Day will not change. This does not exclude the use of the member for Temporary Transfers based on need or availability. Members who opt-in will not be utilized any differently than any other Paramedic.
1. Administration

1.1. Purpose: Allow Firefighters who are not on the authorized Transport Basic list, the ability to opt-in for selected transfer cycle(s) throughout the year in order to staff the CFD EMS Transport Vehicles.

1.2. Responsibility: It shall be the responsibility of each member to know, understand and utilize these procedures as they apply to the situation at hand. It shall further be the responsibility of all Division Officers to train their subordinates in the proper application of these procedures and to implement and enforce the use of these procedures.

1.3. Conflict: This SOP shall not be construed as invalidating, preempting, or superseding any previously issued operating procedure, rule and/or protocol. Conflicts with other SOPs, rules, and/or protocols shall be brought to the immediate attention of the member’s supervisor so that it can be evaluated by the Fire Chief, or designee, and adjusted if necessary.
2. Information

1.4. The Transport Basic list shall consist of the least senior ES Firefighters who have graduated from the training academy. As least senior members are added upon graduation of the training academy, the most senior members on the list are removed in order to maintain an effective number of personnel to operate the current system of fulltime EMS Transport vehicles. When a member is removed, the member still holds the minimum EMT certification with the State of Ohio; however, they will not be used on the EMS Transport vehicle unless they elect to opt-in.
1.5. Those members removed or exempt from the EMS Transport Basic list still have the opportunity to opt-in on a limited basis based on the needs of the Division as determined by the Fire Chief.

1.6. Members can opt-in for a minimum of one transfer cycle. The Fire Chief, based on current needs of the Division, will determine the number of members granted opt-in status.
1.7. The Fire Chief reserves the right to determine the needs of the opt-in program and may limit the number personnel granted or remaining in the opt-in program.

1.8. Those members who have been in downgrade status for a year or less will not be required to go through a retraining period. Those members who have been in downgrade status for longer than a year will be evaluated by the EMS CQI office and/or EMS Supervisors to determine any training needs prior to being placed on the active list.

1.9. Members wishing to opt-in shall submit request (ES-221) through the chainof-command to the Fire Chief by the expiration of the Vacancy list. The effective date of the opt-in will be the effectivedate of the subsequent transfer list or once evaluated by the EMS CQI office and/or EMS Officers and ALL training needs are met (see Section 3.3).
1.10. Members who opt-in will be paid the TransportStipend according to the provisions of the collective bargaining agreement.

1.11. Members opting in shall be considered in the pool of usable Transport Basics until such time they notify the Fire Chief in writing their desire to opt-out, or until notified by the Division that their opt-in status is discontinued.

1.12. Members opting out shall submit request (RT-154) through the chain-ofcommand to the Fire Chief by the expiration of the Vacancy list. The effective date of the opt-out will be the effective date of the subsequent transfer list.
4. Additional

1.13. While active on the Transport Basic authorized list, members will be eligible to work Transport Basic overtime and special duty (according to special duty provisions) as long as the member is proficient in any venue specific specialty training in accordance with current operating procedures.
1.14. The member will be afforded the same overtime privileges as any other Transport Basic with the Division.

1.15. Members electing to opt-in will have their overtime hours adjusted to the average overtime hours of current Transport Basics on their unit. Once the opt-in period is completed, members not renewing their opt-in status will have their overtime hours adjusted back to reflect actual overtime hours worked for the year.

1.16. Unless a petition for change has been granted, a member’s assignment and Kelly Day will not change. This does not exclude the use of the member for Temporary Transfers based on need or availability. Members who opt-in will not be utilized any differently than any other Transport Basics.
1. Administration

1.1. Purpose: There are many duties that the Division must perform in addition to Fire and EMS responsibilities that aids in accomplishing our mission. These duties include filling temporary staffing assignments (TTs), educating the public, instructing Fire/EMS/Rescue courses, and performing a variety of inspections. For tracking and distribution purposes, these duties will be separated in two categories: (1) Station level tasks and (2) Division temporary staffing assignments (TTs). It is the Division’s goal and the purpose of this policy that these duties are assigned and distributed to personnel in a fair and equitable manner.

1.2. Responsibility: It shall be the responsibility of each member to know, understand and utilize these procedures as they apply to the situation at hand. It shall further be the responsibility of all Division Officers to train their subordinates in the proper application of these procedures and to implement and enforce the use of these procedures.

1.3. Conflict: This SOP shall not be construed as invalidating, preempting, or superseding any previously issued operating procedure, rule and/or protocol. Conflicts with other SOPs, rules, and/or protocols shall be brought to the immediate attention of the member’s supervisor so that it can be evaluated by the Fire Chief, or designee, and adjusted if necessary.
2. Implementation
2.1. Station-Level Tasks

1.3.1. Form PL-16 is used to equally allocate Station level tasks. A single sheet is to be used to track the various duties rather than a page for each different type of task. Members will receive credit for each station level task that they perform such as hydrants, buildings, cooking duties, Public Outreach events, and instructing Division training classes.
1.3.2. Members with the least amount of Station leveltasks will be the first choice to perform the next task.

1.3.3. Task lists remain continuous and do not return to zero at year’s end. Members transferring into a station or returning from a long-term absence will be placed on the list with the number of tasks equal to the station average.
2.2. DivisionTemporary Staffing Assignments (TTs)
1.3.4. Form PL-17 is used to equally allocate Division TTs. A single sheet is to be used to track TTs rather than a page for each different type of TT.
1.3.5. Members will receive a TT credit for each TT worked in any capacity at another station (or FAO) for a duration greater than four (4) hours and a maximum of twenty-four (24) hours.
1.3.6. Members will receive a TT credit for staffing the EMS Transport vehicle within one’s assigned station for a duration greater than four (4) hours and a maximum of twenty-four (24) hours.
1.3.7. Members with the least amount of Division TTs will be the first choice for the next TT.

1.3.8. TT lists remain continuous and do not return to zero at year’s end. Members transferring into a station or returning from a long-term absence will be placed on the list with the number of TTs equal to the station average.

1. Administration

1.1. Purpose: The purpose of this procedure is to explain the steps that need to be taken when an employee has not reported to work, has not contacted their employer and equate to an unapproved absence of duty. The employee is then determined to be Absent Without Leave (AWOL; Systems Manual Section 742).

1.2. Responsibility: It shall be the responsibility of each member to know, understand and utilize these procedures as they apply to the situation at hand. It shall further be the responsibility of all Division Officers to train their subordinates in the proper application of these procedures and to implement and enforce the use of these procedures.
2. General

1.3. When a member is not at their assigned reporting location at the beginning of their shift, (Sys Manual Section 406) then the status of AWOL (unapproved absence of duty) may be applied. Before AWOL is determined, the immediate supervisor must verify the said employee is in fact supposed to be there. The supervisor should verify the employee does not have training, vacation, trade, military leave, has been TT’d, etc.

1.4. Once the immediate supervisor determines the employee is in fact AWOL, their Chain of Command should be notified and appropriate staffing should be addressed as needed. At any point the employee returns to work in this process, the Late for Duty Policy (Sys Manual Section 710) shall be followed.
1.5. The immediate supervisor will manage staffing on TeleStaff and be guided by their B/C or Chain of Command.
2. Attempt to Contact Employee

2.1. The immediate supervisor will attempt to contact the employee by using the 1st and 2nd contact phone numbers as stated in TeleStaff or by any other means they have available. The immediate supervisor will make at least two (2) attempts to contact the employee over a 15- to 30-minute time frame. The immediate supervisor will assure the apparatus (if applicable) will stay in service with the appropriate staffing.

2.2. If no response or information is obtained from the employee, the immediate supervisor shall notify their B/C or Chain of Command who will then notify the Deputy Chief. The Deputy Chief’s office will then get an emergency contact name and phone number via FirePoint and attempt to contact the employee or their emergency contact to determine the employee’s whereabouts.
2.3. If no contact or substantial information has been obtained, the Deputy Chief shall coordinate a wellbeing response.
3. EmployeeLives Inside Columbus Jurisdiction
2.4. If an AWOL member lives within the ColumbusDivision of Fire jurisdiction, the Deputy Chief shall send a wellbeing response to the employee’s place of residency on record.

2.5. The Deputy Chief shall make the determination of the needs for the wellbeing response and call the appropriate apparatus with details. The response will be based on any known or unknown information and will respond “signal X”.

1.1. Purpose: To define State Law and the Division’s policy for accepting a newborn child that is voluntarily delivered by a parent that does not intend to keep their child.

1.2. Responsibility: It shall be the responsibility of each member to know, understand and utilize these procedures as they apply to the situation at hand. It shall further be the responsibility of all Division Officers to train their subordinates in the proper application of these procedures and to implement and enforce the use of these procedures.
2. State Law

1.3. Ohio State law exempts a parent from prosecution when they drop off a child that is less the 72 hours old and the child is delivered unharmed to an emergency medical worker, peace officer, or hospital employee.
3. Implementation
3.1. Accepting a Child

1.3.1. The person who accepts a child must first provide any immediate attention the child may need. A Medic Crew shall be called to the dropoff location to evaluate the child for medical needs, which will be treated per protocol.

1.3.2. The person who accepts the child must offer the parent State Form # JFS 1672, VOLUNTARY MEDICAL HISTORY for the collection of the medical history of the child. The form may be filled out and left, or mailed to the address on the back of the format a later date.

1.3.3. A Medic Crew shall transport the child to Children’s Hospital ER for a medical evaluation. Children’s Hospital will coordinate with Franklin County Children Services the transfer of care for the child.
1.3.4. The CFD member that accepted the child shall notify Franklin County Children Services’ office.
1.4. Prohibited Activity
1.4.1. State law provides that no person may do the following with respect to a parent who voluntarily delivers a child:
1.4.1.1. Coerce or otherwise try to force the parent into revealing their identity.
3.1.1.1. Pursue or follow the parent after they leave.
3.1.1.2. Coerce or otherwise try to force a parent not to leave the child.
1.4.1.2. Coerce or otherwise try to force the parent to complete all or any part of the medical information forms provided to the parent by the person to whom the parent delivers the child.
1.4.1.3. Coerce or otherwise try to force the parent to accept materials that describe services available to assist parents and newborns.
1.5. Anonymity Right
1.5.1. The parent has the right to remain anonymousand to leave at any time after delivering the child.

1.5.2. The right to anonymitydoes not exist if the child has suffered any physical or mental wound, injury, disability, or condition of a nature that reasonably indicates abuse or neglect of the child. In this case, the parent is subject to arrest and prosecution.
3.2. Child Abuse or Neglect
1.5.3. If a child has been abused, neglected, or delivered in a manner otherthan as specified:
1.5.3.1. Provide any medical services that are necessary to protect the physical health or safety of the child.
1.5.3.2. Notify the police. The parent does not have the right to remain anonymous and may be subject to arrest.
1.5.3.3. The person who delivers the child may be forced to reveal the identity of the child’s parents and may be pursued orfollowed.
1.5.3.4. The person to whom the child is delivered must attempt to identify and pursue the person who delivered the child.
1.5.3.5. The person who delivers the child will not have civil or criminal immunity as provided by law.
3.3. Reclaiming a Child

1.5.4. State law provides a way for the parent to reclaim their child up to the point of final adoption. The county’s child welfare agency will conduct an assessment of the parent to ensure the child’s safety.
1. Administration

1.1. Purpose: The purpose of this document is to describe the procedure for authorizing a person who is not a sworn member of the Division to ride along as a student or observer. Consideration will be given to students, nurses and physicians enrolled in a school or hospital affiliated program. Exceptions may be granted by the Fire Chief or the Chief’s designee.

1.2. Responsibility: It shall be the responsibility of each member to know, understand and utilize these procedures as they apply to the situation at hand. It shall further be the responsibility of all Division Officers to train their subordinates in the proper application of these procedures and to implement and enforce the use of these procedures.

1.3. Background: The Rider program allows individuals, who have been authorized, to ride Columbus Division of Fire emergency and fire vehicles with Division personnel responding to emergencies. This opportunity allows the rider to gain insight to the profession of a firefighter and to experience the challenges and rewards Division members face. It is also an opportunity for people in the Fire/EMS fields outside the division to increase their knowledge and expand their horizons by seeing how the Columbus Division of Fire operates.
1.4. Exceptions:Exceptions to this policy may be granted by the Fire Chief or the Chief’s designee on a case-by-case basis (e.g., political officeholders/candidates, media, and VIPs).
2. Definitions
1.5. Rider – A person who is not a sworn memberof the Division of Fire and will be categorized as either an observer or student.
1.6. Observer – A rider whose purpose is to learn and experience how the Division of Fire operates in providing service to the public.

1.7. Student – A rider whose purpose is to not only observe, but to gain knowledge and skills that are used in Fire andEMS. All students must have prior approval from the Training Academy to ride divisional apparatus.
3. Permission
1.8. All Rider requestsmust be approved by the EmergencyServices Deputy Chief before an individual is allowed to participate in the Rider program.

1.9. All potential Riders must first complete a Rider Application Form, Waiver & Release of Liability form, and Confidentiality Statement in the presence of the officer in charge of the station where the ride is being requested. All three of these forms shall then be communicated through the chain-of-command to the appropriate deputy chief for approval.
1.9.1. Applications will only be considered if the applicant meets the following:
1.9.1.1. Presenta government issued picture Identification at the time of application (e.g., driver’s license, passport, etc.).
3.1.1.1. Be at least 18 years or older.
3.1.1.2. Sign a Waiver & Release of Liability form.
3.1.1.3. Sign a Confidentiality Statement.
1.9.2. Approval is limited to one Rider per vehicle at a time. When multiple requestsare received, preference will be given to an applicant thatmeets the following:
1.9.2.1. Be a physician or nurse actively working in an emergency department.
3.1.1.4. Be an active member of a mutual aid department.
3.1.1.5. Be a member of an out-of-town EMS system (one time basis).
3.1.1.6. Be an EMT student.
3.1.2. Applicants will not be permitted to ride if:
1.9.2.2. Applicant is determined to have a record as a convicted felon, sex offender, or any other history that would compromise the trust instilled in the Division of Fire by the public.
1.10. Requests that do not meet the above criteria will be approved by the EmergencyServices Deputy Chief on a case-by-case basis. This authority does not extend to exceptions mentioned in 1.4 above.
1.11. In all cases, completed applications, Waiver & Release of Liability forms, and Confidentiality Statements shall be forwarded through channels to Emergency Services Assistant Chief (ES-1).
1.11.1. The original forms will remain at ES-1’s office until permitted to be destroyed per the Records Retention Schedule.
2. Clothing and Appearance

2.1. All Riders shall be appropriately dressed at all times. The officer or firefighterin-charge shall have the authority to deny participation to any rider who is inappropriately dressed, or in a condition that may compromise the safety or best interest of the Division, the assigned shift, or the Rider.
3.2. The Rider will wear:
3.2.1. Shoes – Closed-toe with a good non-slip sole.
2.1.1. Pants – Long pants that sit at waist. Undergarments shall not be visible when in a normal standing position. No Jeans.
3.2.2. Shirt – Solid color dress or polo style. No T-shirts.
2.2. Participants from a school or hospital program may wear their class uniform if approved by the battalion chief. Scrubs are permitted for hospital personnel.
3.3. Jackets – Dark solid color recommended. Weather dictating.
3.4. Minimal Jewelry. No nose, tongue or eyebrow piercings will be permitted.
2.3. Hair – Long hair shall be pulled back as to not interfere with Division activities or present an undue safety hazard.

2.4. Ballistic Vests – In the event that a Rider is on a vehicle that is dispatched to a shooting or stabbing and the crew is required to don a ballistic vest, the rider will also don a ballistic vest, even though the rider is required to remain inside the assigned vehicle for the entire duration of the incident.
4. Rider Duties and Restrictions
2.5. The normal approved ride-along hours are from 0800 hours to 2200 hours.
2.5.1. Exceptions to these hour restrictions may include those in an approved school or hospital affiliated program or on a case-by-case basis as determined by the on-duty deputy chief.

2.6. At no time will the participant become involved in assisting during an event of physical violence from another person. It is permissible for the participant to use Division communication equipment to contact the Fire Alarm Office to request assistance.

2.7. No Rider will be permitted to carry any weapons at any time while on city property or while riding on Division vehicles, regardless of licenses orpermits they possess. This does not include a pocket knife of a reasonable size. Reasonableness will be determined by the officer or firefighter in charge.

2.8. At no time will a participant be allowed to carry any electronics while riding Division vehicles. Cell phones, cameras, recorders, or any other means of audio/visual recording shall be left at the station or in the participant’s personal vehicle. Media requests will be handled by the Division Public Information Officer or the PIO designee.

2.9. Participants acknowledge that the Division of Fire is a paramilitary organization and that during emergency runs it is accepted that when an officer gives and order or direction, it is to be followed immediately and without question. The participant agrees to abide by the direction of the officer or firefighter-in- charge without discussion.
5. Safety Responsibilities

2.10. Under the direction of the officer or in-charge person, all Riders are required to abide by all divisional safety policies and procedures (e.g., seat belt usage, high-visibility vest when applicable, accountability, universal precautions).
2.11. The officer or firefighter-in-charge shall take every precaution to prevent the participant from becoming physically involved in or assisting in the following types on incidents:
5.1.1. Crime Scenes
5.1.2. Violent patients
5.1.3. Patients with known infectious diseases
5.1.4. Fireground operations
5.1.5. Situations involving or likely to involve the use of guns
2.11.1. Other activities that are known to orlikely to increase the participant’s risk of exposure

2.12. If a vehicle with a Ride-Along participant is dispatched on a call that the officer or firefighter-in-charge feels may result in the crew becoming immediately involved in a hazardous situation, the participant shall be instructed to remain in the vehicle. It is permissible for the officer or firefighter-in-charge to leave the participant at the station if in quarters at the time of dispatch.

2.13. If, at any time, the officer in charge of the station where the ride is being requested believes there is justifiable reason to either deny and/or suspend the Rider request, he/she has the authority to do so and shall immediately notify the on-duty deputy chief through channels. Additionally, a letter of explanation shall be submitted through channels to the Fire Chief.
3. Forms
5.2. Rider Application Form (ES-215e)
5.3. Waiver& Release of Liability form (ES-216e)
5.4. Confidentiality Statement form (ES-217e)

6.1. Columbus Division of Fire Systems Manual Sections 414.00 to 414.16
6.2. Columbus Division of Fire Forms ES-215e, ES-216e, ES-217e

1. Administration

1.1. Purpose: This policy establishes the Division of Fire’s social media use, procedures, and protocols; which are intended to mitigate associated risks from the use of this technology where possible. This policy is not meant to address one particular form of social media, rather social media in general, as technology changes.

1.2. Responsibility: It shall be the responsibility of each member to know, understand and utilize these procedures as they apply to the situation at hand. It shall further be the responsibility of all Division Officers to train their subordinates in the proper application of these procedures and to implement and enforce the use of these procedures.

1.3. Conflict: This SOP shall not be construed as invalidating, preempting, or superseding any previously issued operating procedure, rule and/or protocol. Conflicts with other SOPs, rules, and/or protocols shall be brought to the immediate attention of the member’s supervisor so that it can be evaluated by the Fire Chief, or designee, and adjusted if necessary.
1. Definitions
1.4. Pages – “Pages” is the specific portion of a social media website where content is displayed, and managed by an individual or individuals with administrator rights.
1.5. Post – “Post” is the content an individual shares on a social media site or the act of publishing content on a site.

1.6. Social Media – A category of Internet-based resources that integrate usergenerated content and user participation. This includes, but is not limited to, social networking sites (e.g., Facebook, MySpace), micro blogging sites (e.g., Twitter, Nixle), photo- and video-sharing sites (e.g., Flickr, Snap Chat, Instagram, YouTube), wikis (e.g., Wikipedia), blogs, and news sites (e.g., Digg, Reddit).
1.7. Speech – Expression of communication of thoughts or opinions in spoken words, in writing, by expressive conduct, symbolism, photographs, video, or related forms of communication.
2. Information
1.8. Social media provides valuable assistance to Division personnel with meeting community outreach, solving problems, conducting investigations, and fire prevention.
1.9. The Division endorses the exchange of information via social media to enhance communication, encourage collaboration, and foster productivity.

1.10. The Division recognizes the role that these tools play in the personal lives of some Division personnel. The personal use of social media can have bearing on Division personnel in their official capacity. This policy provides prohibitions on the use of social media by Division personnel where such is the case.
3. PolicyStatements
3.1. On-dutyuse representing the Division of Fire:

1.10.1. Division social media sites or pages, including but not limited to, Official Division pages and Station pages, shall be approved by the Fire Chief or his/her designee and shall be administered by the Public Information Officer or his/her designee. The Public Information Office or his/her designee may delegate management responsibilities of social media sites or pages to approved offices.
1.10.2. Social media pages shall clearly indicate they are maintained by the Division and shall have Division contact information prominently displayed.
1.10.3. Social media content shall adhere to applicable laws, regulations, and policies, including all information technology policies.
1.10.4. Social media pages shall state that the opinions expressed by visitors to the page(s) do not reflect the opinions of the Division.

1.10.5. Pages shall clearly indicate that posted content will be monitored and that the Division reserves the right to remove any content for reasons including, but not limited, comments that contain obscenities, off-topic comments, and personal attacks.
1.10.6. Pages shall clearly indicate that any content posted or submitted for posting is subject to public disclosure.
1.10.7. Personnel representing the Division via social media outlets shall identify themselves as a member of the Division.
1.10.8. Division personnel shall observe and abide by all copyright, trademark, and service mark restrictions in posting materials to social media.
1.10.9. Personnel representing the Division via social media outlets shall not conduct private business on the social media site.
1.10.10. Personal Use of social media – Division personnel are free to express themselves as private citizens on social media sites to the degree that their speech does not:
1.10.10.1. Violate any other Division of Fire Rules of Conduct, Policy, Systems Manual, Directive, or City Work Rule.
3.1.1.1. Impairworking relationships within the Division of Fire.
1.10.10.2. Demean,ridicule, or personally attack employees of the Division of Fire (see Systems Manual Section 204).
1.10.10.3. Impede or interfere with their own or that of another Division employee’s ability to perform their job requirements.

1.10.11. Personnel shall not post pictures or otherwise identify other Division of Fire personnel assigned to covert assignments if the posting could identify the covert personnel as a firefighter (see Digital Imagery SOP 04-05-08).
1.10.12. Division personnel shall not post comments, pictures, or video of emergency scenes that could be under investigation.

1.10.13. Division personnel shall not post comments, pictures, or video of emergency scenes that would violate HIPAA laws (the HIPAA Privacy Rule Policy can be found in “Guidelines” in the Responsoft Administrative protocol).
1.10.14. Division personnel shall not engage in speech that may undermine or impeach a Division employee’s testimony in criminal proceedings.
1.10.15. Nothing stated above shall prohibit (a) the use of social media to discuss matters associated with terms/conditions of employment or (b) constitutionally protected speech.
1. Administration

1.1. Purpose: The purpose of this policy is to protect nonpublic employee data, medical patients, the public, the operations of the Fire Department, and public confidence in the Fire Department and its employees. This policy establishes the Division of Fire’s position on the management of photographs and electronic images taken by Division personnel while providing guidance on its administration. This policy is not meant to address one particular form of photography/digital imagery, rather photography/digital imagery in general, as technology changes.

1.2. Responsibility: It shall be the responsibility of each member to know, understand and utilize these procedures as they apply to the situation at hand. It shall further be the responsibility of all Division Officers to train their subordinates in the proper application of these procedures and to implement and enforce the use of these procedures.

1.3. Conflict: This SOP shall not be construed as invalidating, preempting, or superseding any previously issued operating procedure, rule and/or protocol. Conflicts with other SOPs, rules, and/or protocols shall be brought to the immediate attention of the member’s supervisor so that it can be evaluated by the Fire Chief, or designee, and adjusted if necessary.
2. Definitions

1.4. Images – “Images” include photographs, digital photographs, digital images, video recordings, or electronic files containing a graphic image or series of images, as well as any physical or digital reproduction or copies of digital photographs, digital images, video recordings, or files.

1.5. Imaging Device – “Imaging Device” includes any device capable of producing an image or digital image, including but not limited to a camera, cellular phone, video camera, helmet camera, digital camera or digital camcorder.

1.6. Social Media – A category of Internet-based resources that integrate usergenerated content and user participation. This includes, but is not limited to, social networking sites (e.g., Facebook, MySpace), micro blogging sites (e.g., Twitter, Nixle), photo- and video-sharing sites (e.g., Flickr, Snap Chat, Instagram, YouTube), wikis (e.g., Wikipedia), blogs, and news sites (e.g., Digg, Reddit).
1.7. Speech – Expression of communication of thoughts or opinions in spoken words, in writing, by expressive conduct, symbolism, photographs, video, or related forms of communication.
3. PolicyStatements
1.8. Scope – To assure professionalism and the privacy rights of patients, fire victims, and the public that we serve.

1.9. Under no circumstances will Division personnel be allowed to use a personal imaging device (including helmet cameras) while at any incident without the expressed written permission of the Fire Chief or his/her designee.

1.9.1. All approved incident scene images shall be for incident documentation, evidence, training, investigation, and/or public relations only, and taken by or with the approval of the Incident Commander in charge of the scene.
1.9.2. Each Bureau Head will maintain a list of personnel/positionsapproved to take on-scene images.
1.9.3. All approved incident scene images shall be taken using approved Division equipment, oras approved by the Fire Chief or his/her designee.
1.9.4. The taking of images shall not interfere with nor delay operational activities, unless otherwise approved by to the Incident Commander.

1.9.5. Authorized images taken by a member in the course and scope of their duties may not be used, printed, copied, scanned, e-mailed, posted, shared, reproduced or distributed in any manner without the expressed written permission of the Fire Chief or his/her designee.

1.9.6. This prohibition includes the posting of any Division of Fire photographs on personal Web sites such as, but not restricted to: Facebook, MySpace, YouTube, other public safety agency websites, or e-mailed to friends, relatives or colleagues.

1.10. Photographs, digital images, and/or videos on personal imaging devices are permitted at non-emergency scenes and shall conform to the Division’s Social Media Policy. Consideration shall be given to security issues when in Division facilities.
1.11. Personal use of the Division’s cameras or digital imaging devices is prohibited.
1.12. Violation of this policy, or failure to permit inspection of any device covered in this policy, may result in disciplinary action.
4. Image Storage

1.13. All digital images referenced in paragraph 3.2, above, shall be downloaded from the imaging device as soon as possible after the image is created into the Division’s digital image secured database, as established by the Division’s Public Information Graphics Technician.
4.1.1. All images shall be cataloged on the Division’s photo log.
1.13.1. Digital image file names shall be left in the unaltered default name given by the digital imaging equipment being used. Description of the images shall be made on the Division’s photo log.
1.13.2. After such images are properly downloaded, the digital images/videos shall be securely erased from on the digital imaging device’s memory.

1.13.3. Division personnel shall not delete, edit, crop, lighten/darken, blur, alter, etc. any original photograph, digital image, and/or video in any way without the expressed written permission of the Fire Chief or his/her designee.

1.13.4. If permission to alter a photograph, digital image, and/or video is granted, the original imagery shall not be altered in any way, and any copies that are altered shall be appropriately identified and documented as to being an altered copy.

1.13.5. The details of the alteration including what was done (cropped, lightened, darkened, etc.), the name and division id of the member performing the alteration, and the time and date of the alteration, shall be noted in writing and preserved with the original photo log.

1.13.6. If an original image is deleted, lost, or tampered with in any way, personnel having knowledge of this shall immediately document the circumstances and forward through his/her chain-of-command.

1.14. Non-digital images taken on Division equipment, including negatives, prints, slides, etc. shall be forward to the Division’s records office. If non-digital images are not developed, the undeveloped film shall be transferred to the Division’s record office.
5. PublicRecord Compliance

1.15. All Division images containing individually identifiable patient information (e.g., license plates, tattoos, address, etc.) are covered by HIPAA privacy laws and must be protected in the same manner as patient care reports and documentation.

1.16. Division of Fire imagesare subject to State ofOhio public records laws. Any content maintained on the Division of Fire’s social media pages, that are related to Division matters, including a list of subscribers, posted communications, and all images/videos are public records.
1.17. Record Retention and Management.State ofOhio law and City of Columbus Division of Fire records retention schedules apply to all Division images/videos regardless of ownership of the device.
1.18. Division’s Public Information Officer shall respond to any records request for public records including requests for images.
2. Use of Images
2.1. Personnel shall not seek permission to post Division images without first following the procedures outlined above.

2.2. Once the procedures outlined above are completed, the Fire Chief or his/her designee may approve posting when images are provided in advance of any posting and after they have been reviewed to ensure that images comply with standards, regulations, and/or interfere with ongoing investigations.
1. Administration
1.1. Purpose: The purpose of this standard operating procedure is to give guidance and direction when dealing with bed bugs.

1.2. Responsibility: It shall be the responsibility of each member to know, understand and utilize these procedures as they apply to the situation at hand. It shall further be the responsibility of all Division Officers to train their subordinates in the proper application of these procedures and to implement and enforce the use of these procedures.
2. Background
1.3. A resurgence of bed bugs has emerged within the United States including Central Ohio. The risk of exposure to bed bugs exists in our buildings, vehicles, and on runs.
3. Prevention Strategies
3.1. Limit the number of individuals exposed.
3.2. Limitmovement of items into and out of suspected areas or vehicles.
1.4. Bunkergear should stay in the apparatus bay and not be brought into sleeping or common areas.
1.5. Vacuum beds, bedrooms, sofas, and chairs weekly orfollowing any potential bed bug exposure to these areas.
1.6. Care should be taken to seal up (trash bag & tied off) and dispose of vacuum contents to prevent bugs from escaping from the vacuum and being reintroduced.
1.7. Take steps to minimize clutter, especially near sleeping areas where clutter would provide hiding places for bed bugs, such as lockers.
1.8. Storing items in sealable containers or bags will eliminate hiding places for bugs.

1.9. Mattress and box spring bed bug proof covers should be kept on all Division beds and checked weekly, with attention to checking all sides of the mattress or box spring. Damaged or missing covers should be reported to Supply for replacement.
1.10. Store personal bedding in plastic bag or containers that can be sealed between uses.
3.3. Dutyuniforms should be stored laundered at the fire station when practical.

1.11. Uniforms should not be taken home. They should be bagged, sealed, and washed separate from personal laundry. Care should be taken to ensure that the bagged uniforms are placed directly from the sealed bag into the laundry. Follow the “Bed Bug Guidelines and Prevention” document in the “Common Share Folder”.
1.12. Drying on high heat for at least 30 minutes has been shown to be an effective method to kill bed bugs.
2. Action Plan Following Exposure
3.4. Notify station in-charge person.

2.1. Station in-charge person shall follow or designate a person to follow the “Bed Bug Guidelines and Prevention” document that can be found on the intranet in the “Common Share Folder” in a folder named “Bed Bug Response Information”.

2.2. The “Bed Bug Guidelines and Prevention” document provides instruction on how to handle a bed bug discovery involving several types of situations. The document is separate from the SOP in order to allow for frequent revision as necessary.
2.3. Document exposure in the Station Smooth Log and create a Lucity work order.
2.3.1. A significant exposure shall be reported on a Personal Exposure Report under Division Forms.
2.3.2. A significant exposure is defined as handling of or in very close proximity to a patient or area with multiple bed bug stages, multiple bed bug areas, and/or eggs.
2.4. Complete a Health & Safety Report (RI-173e)if found in the station or vehicle.
2.5. Capture bugs for identification/confirmation when possible. Use clear tape or a plastic baggie with care not to make the bug unrecognizable.

2.6. If bed bugs are found on your clothing, remove clothes and shoes: bag and seal them. Bagged clothing suspected of infestation with bed bugs should not be taken home, but should be laundered at the station or sent to the Division laundry technician for proper treatment.
2.7. Specific prevention and recommended actions can be found in the “Bed Bug Guidelines and Prevention” document found in the “Common Share Folder” in a folder named “Bed Bug Response Information”.

2.8. Questions and/or concerns regarding bed bugs should be directed to SO2. 05-01-04.t: Audit of Firefighter, Fire Safety Inspector, EMS, and
p: 1. Administration
1.1. Purpose: To identify the proper procedure to fulfill the requirements of certification audit by the State of Ohio.

1.2. Responsibility: It shall be the responsibility of each member to know, understand and utilize these procedures as they apply to the situation at hand. It shall further be the responsibility of all Division Officers to train their subordinates in the proper application of these procedures and to implement and enforce the use of these procedures.
1. General

1.3. The State of Ohio Division of EMS currently audits Firefighter, Fire Safety Inspector, EMS, and Instructor certification renewals. Ten percent of all certificate renewals each month are randomly selected for audit.

1.4. These audits require a certification holder to complete forms provided by the state and submit documentation of continuing education that an individual has received during the certification period for the requested certificate. The Division of Fire provides a Distance Learning Platform to assist personnel in completing and tracking the needed continuing education for Firefighter II, Fire Safety Inspector, EMS, and Instructor certifications.

1.5. Personnel who are being audited will receive a letter or an email from the State of Ohio Division of EMS at the address they have registered with the State. This communication will indicate which certification is being audited and the continuing education documentation required.

1.6. EMS and EMS Instructor audits will be handled through Training 23 (EMS Training Records Specialist). These audits require the signature of the certificate holder and the EMS Education Manager. Members will be directed by Training 23 in the completion of these forms and the documentation of EMS Continuing Education. Members are required to drop off the audit forms at the Division of Fire Training complex room 220 within seven (7) days of receipt for signatures. After the forms have been reviewed and signed, you will pick them up for mailing to the state.

1.7. Firefighter, Fire Safety Inspector, Fire Instructor, and Fire Safety Inspector Instructor audits will be handled through Training 30 (In-Service Training). These audits require the signature of the certificate holder and the Fire Chief’s designee. Members will be directed by Training 30 in the completion of these forms and the documentation of appropriate Continuing Education. Members are required to drop off the audit forms at the Division of Fire Training complex room 223 for signatures within seven (7) days of receipt. After the forms have been reviewed and signed, you will pick them up for mailing to the state.

1.8. While the Division will attempt to assist any member being audited, the audit and certification is a matter between the State of Ohio and the member. The Division assumes no responsibility and it remains the member’s full responsibility to maintain all required certifications.
1. Administration

1.1. Purpose: The purpose of this operating procedure is to identify the procedures that MUST be followed by all uniformed personnel who have had any of their federal, state and/or city certifications, related to their employment with the City of Columbus Division of Fire, suspended, restricted, downgraded, revoked, or may be facing disciplinary action from the agency in which the certification(s) is issued.

1.2. Responsibility: It shall be the responsibility of each member to know, understand and utilize these procedures as they apply to the situation at hand. It shall further be the responsibility of all Division Officers to train their subordinates in the proper application of these procedures and to implement and enforce the use of these procedures.
1. General

1.3. Members who have had any of their federal, state and/or city certifications, related to their employment with the City of Columbus Division of Fire, suspended, restricted, downgraded, revoked, or may be facing disciplinary action from the agency in which the certification(s) is issued shall immediately notify the Fire Chief in writing.

1.4. Members who have knowledge that another Division member has had their federal, state and/or city certifications, related to their employment with the City of Columbus Division of Fire, suspended, restricted, downgraded, revoked, or facing disciplinary action from the agency in which the certification(s) is issued is also under duty to immediately notify the Fire Chief in writing of this fact.

1.5. In addition to any discipline associated with the loss of member’s certification(s), failure to report the loss of certification(s) as stated above may result in a disciplinary action for failure to report.
1.6. After notification, the member may be immediately placed on administrative duties, pending an investigation and review by the Fire Chief or designee.

1.7. Because the loss of any certification may immediately impact the member’s ability to perform job duties, an expedited hearing with the Fire Chief or designee will be scheduled to evaluate the underlying facts that caused the change to the member’s certification.

1.8. The Fire Chief or designee may consider all factors associated with the loss of certification, including but not limited to, the impact the loss will have on the members ability to perform job duties, the cause of the loss, and the length of time the certification(s) is suspended or restricted. These situations will be evaluated on a case-by-case basis.
1.1. Discipline may include all remedies, up to and including, termination.
1.2. Membersmay be responsible for any costs associated with recertification.

1.9. This SOP shall not be construed as invalidating, preempting, or superseding any previously issued regulation, operating procedure, work rule and/or protocol. Conflicts withany previously issued regulation,operating procedure, work rule and/or protocol shall be brought to the attention of the Administrative Assistant Chief through the chain-of-command. Potential conflicts will be evaluated and adjusted if necessary.
1. Administration
1.1. Purpose: To provide guidelines for notifying the Training Bureau of "significant" training.

1.2. Responsibility: It shall be the responsibility of each member to know, understand and utilize these procedures as they apply to the situation at hand. It shall further be the responsibility of all Division Officers to train their subordinates in the proper application of these procedures and to implement and enforce the use of these procedures.
2. General

1.3. Any person/company conducting "significant" training shall notify Training 30 at the Training Bureau three (3) duty days or nine (9) calendar days prior to the date on which the training is scheduled to occur.
1.3.1. This notification will allow us to provide you with any needed assistance as well as allow us to track the types and quality of training that is occurring within the Division.

1.3.2. Notification shall include a TA-510, outline, safety plan, and sign-in sheet. This packet can be found in the Common Share folder under "Training". Courses that require certification also require that the member's file be updated upon successful completion of the course.
1.3.3. Upon receipt of the completed sign-in sheet, the Training Bureau will be responsible for updating those files.

1.4. Examples of"significant" training include, but are not limited to: training fires, AARF pit fires, HazMat training, multiple-company evolutions, rescue operations, bomb and arson training, high-rise evolutions, etc. The Training Bureau will track all training of this type in the future.

1.5. If you are not sure if the training that you intend to conduct is "significant" training, or if you have other questions, please contact Training 30 at 75330. 1. Administration
1.1. Purpose: Vehicle maintenance procedures.

1.1. Responsibility: It shall be the responsibility of each member to know, understand and utilize these procedures as they apply to the situation at hand. It shall further be the responsibility of all Division Officers to train their subordinates in the proper application of these procedures and to implement and enforce the use of these procedures.
2. Procedures

1.2. When a need for maintenance to any Division of Fire vehicle has been identified, document the maintenance item in the vehicle log book (minor or major repair). Then contact Fleet at 614-645-6273 or Maintenance 19, East Garage Supervisor, on 10-Maintenance and be guided by his or her directions.
2.1. The reporting process for all vehicle maintenance is as follows:

1.2.1. Once the vehicle driver discovers needed repairs, he/she will create a service request by filling out the ER-99, Service Request Form located under Division Forms. It is imperative that all of the information on the form is filled out.

1.2.2. Once the form is completed, save the form and email a copy of the form to the Apparatus Liaison Officer (ALO). The email address, CFDServiceRequests@columbus.gov, can found by typing “CFD”in the global address book in Microsoft Outlook.
1.2.3. In addition, for emergency service vehicles (ES), if the vehicle is out of service (OOS) or the vehicle has been requested at Fleet:
1.2.3.1. The driver shall notify his or her battalion chief and the FAO of their status. This should be done by voice and by pressing the OOS button on their MDC.
1.2.3.2. The driver shall also type the perceived problem on the OOS screen to document the maintenance problem.

1.2.4. If the need for maintenance occurred while out of the station or office, an ER-99 form shall be completed and emailed to the ALO, as indicated above, as soon as returning to the station or office.

1.3. All members are to continue to comply with the applicable sections of the Systems Manual and SOP 06-01-02, Apparatus OOS Criteria and 06-01-03, Apparatus Tag Out Procedures in regards to the responsibilities to perform station-level vehicle maintenance. Contact the ALO at 74467 or 74468 if you have questions.

1. Administration
1.1. Purpose: To provide a procedure for readily identifying apparatus that are out of service and laid in for repair at Fleet Maintenance.

1.2. Responsibility: It shall be the responsibility of each member to know, understand and utilize these procedures as they apply to the situation at hand. It shall further be the responsibility of all Division Officers to train their subordinates in the proper application of these procedures and to implement and enforce the use of these procedures.
1. Procedures

1.3. Every time Division apparatus are laid in for repair at the Fleet Maintenance Shop, the apparatus shall be identified as out of service by displaying an Out of Service sign in the driver’s window. All apparatus located at Fleet Maintenance shall be considered out of service, unless determined otherwise by the Fleet Shift Supervisor. When repairs are completed, any apparatus being picked up from Fleet Maintenance will need the approval of the Shift Supervisor prior to leaving the premises.

1.4. Any time a Division vehicle is taken to Fleet Maintenance and it cannot be repaired at that time, the Fleet Maintenance Supervisor, or designee, will place an Out of Service sign in the driver’s window to identify the apparatus as unfit for duty.

1.5. The Out of Service sign will denote to all members that the apparatus is unavailable, waiting forrepairs, and is unfit forduty. Under no circumstances can this out-of-service sign be removed by anyone other than the Fleet Maintenance Supervisor or designee.

1.6. Once a vehicle has been repaired and is ready for use, the Shift Supervisor will notify station personnel, preferably an Officer or Acting Officer, that the vehicle is repaired and ready to be put back in service. When reporting to Fleet to pick up apparatus, station personnel must check in with the Shift Supervisor. The person picking up the vehicle must perform an inspection to assure that it is ready for service. At that time, the shift Supervisor or designee will have OOS signage removed, before changing over or returning to quarters.
1.7. Any laid-in vehicle found at Fleet Maintenancewithout an Out ofService sign must still be considered unusable, until it has been cleared by the Fleet Maintenance Supervisor, or designee.
