602.22 The size of the numbers used on the various sizes of hose shall be the height of the hose when hose is laid flat and shall be 1/4 inch in width. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies TOOL AND EQUIPMENT MARKING DATA

602.24 All ladders, tools, and other equipment assigned to the various companies shall be appropriately marked by using the authorized marking pens. In order to properly mark those items which are black or have other dark surfaces, it shall be necessary to paint a block background (using aluminum paint) on the area in which the identifying number is to be installed. Due to the non-porous surfaces of some items of this type, vigorous scrubbing or cleaning may remove the markings, thereby necessitating the periodic renewal of such markings. When marking tools and equipment, care shall be taken so as not to obscure the permanent brass tag number. The size of the company numbers marked on tools and equipment shall be such that they are readily visible. The style of each numeral shall conform to that of the authorized sample.
602.26 Ladders will be marked on the outside of both beams, approximately eighteen inches (18") above the butt of the ladder.
602.28 All other tools and fittings shall be marked where plainly visible in an area subject to the least amount of wear. APPARATUS-MAINTENANCE PROCEDURES
604.00 Company Commanders and other Division members’ assigned Division vehicles shall be responsible for the proper care and maintenance of such vehicles.

604.02 Care and maintenance of Division vehicles shall be performed on two basic levels: fire station maintenance and shop level maintenance. General guidelines concerning the two levels are included in the following paragraphs. In situations where questions arise as to who should perform specific duties or operations, appropriate communications shall be forwarded through channels to the Chief of the Division, requesting clarification of any disputed procedure. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies

604.04 Of major importance at the fire station level is a regular program of vehicle inspection and preventive maintenance. Included in station level procedures are activities such as minor repairs and adjustments, lubrication, bulb replacement, and general cleaning tasks.
604.06 Shop level maintenance will include repair, replacement, and adjustment procedures of a major nature or requiring knowledge and/or equipment not normally available at the fire station level.

604.08 In keeping with the provisions of this section, regular or temporarily assigned drivers of Division vehicles shall be responsible, under the direction of their immediate supervisors, for the proper care, station level maintenance, and operational readiness of their vehicles.

604.12 The drivers of vehicles shall be required to become familiar with - and maintain a working knowledge of - the various systems, components, lubrication points, reservoir fill points (hydraulic oil, fuel, and water), battery, servicing requirements, and other pertinent operating characteristics of their respective vehicles. Manuals and information sheets provided by the apparatus manufacturers, the Training Bureau and the Support Services Bureau, together with Division-wide preventive maintenance and minor repair instruction programs are to be followed in the performance of station level maintenance. The driver/operator should be able to anticipate and recognize any potential mechanical problems. (Revised 12/31/15) Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies

604.14 At the beginning of each work shift, immediately after roll call, the drivers or operators of Division Apparatus (i.e., engines, ladders, rescues, etc.), with the aid of other company members, shall inspect the apparatus in order to ensure its operational readiness. The following items are to be checked, and proper entries made in the apparatus log book; a. Fuel Tanks: Fuel tanks shall be maintained above 1/2 full throughout the work shift. b. Oil Level: Add proper oil when necessary to maintain level within the “safe” range. c. Radiator: Maintain approximately one inch above top of core tubes. Use a vehicle manufacturer recommended coolant or coolant mixture. d. Batteries: Maintain water level above plates. Always use battery syringe when adding water. Never over-fill and keep the top wiped clean. Terminals shall be kept clean and tight. e. Tires: Conduct visual check. f. Brake Air Tanks: Build pressure when necessary. Bleed water from tanks daily during freezing weather. g. Water Tanks: Should be full. h. Lights: Check all emergency and service lights. (Revised 12/31/15)

604.15 On Monday of each week, drivers or operators of all Division vehicles except chief's cars, bureau and station trucks, and emergency medical and rescue service vehicles shall perform a visual check of the underside of their assigned vehicles. Other company members will assist when necessary. Such things as loose fittings; broken or damaged lines; leaks involving water, fuel, or lubricants; frayed or broken wires; or any other readily apparent condition shall be reported to the proper supervisor immediately and repaired, without delay, by the driver or operator if possible, as shall be determined by the officer in charge. Enter all such repairs in the vehicle’s apparatus log book. If the repair cannot be accomplished effectively at the station level, the Maintenance Shop shall be contacted. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies

604.16 Officers in charge of all Division vehicles except chief’s cars, bureau and station cars, and emergency medical service vehicles, shall have a visual check of the underside of their assigned apparatus performed each Monday. Items such as loose fittings, broken or damaged lines, leaks involving fuel, water or lubricants, frayed or damaged wires, or any other readily apparent conditions should be repaired at the station level or referred to the Maintenance Shop as conditions warrant. All problems and repairs shall be recorded in the apparatus log book.

604.18 After each fire or emergency run, vehicles shall be checked for any damage or malfunction that might prevent a safe response on subsequent emergency runs. When conducting the check, particular attention should be given those items mentioned in the preceding paragraphs.

604.20 The driver or operator shall be aware of all regularly scheduled preventive maintenance needs, and shall advise his/her immediate superior whenever equipment or supplies are needed. Drivers or other Division members responsible for Division vehicles shall advise their immediate superiors when shop level maintenance is needed. Personnel who use Division vehicles on a regular basis for daytime duties and activities shall schedule such vehicles for routine maintenance procedures as needed. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies

604.22 Some of the regularly scheduled tests and preventive maintenance operations to be performed at the station level are listed below. All operational tests performed on a regular basis shall be done on Monday. a. Check air pressure in tires (weekly). b. Check wheel lug bolts for tightness (weekly - notify Maintenance Shop if loose) c. Test parallel/series valve and governor or relief valve (weekly). d. Check priming pump oil level (weekly and after each use). e. Lubricate intake and outlet valves (monthly). f. Oil outlet and drain valve linkage systems (monthly). g. Operate and climb aerial ladder (weekly). h. Clean ladder cable and fittings (bi-monthly). i. Lubricate ladder cable and fittings (bi-monthly). j. Lubricate turntable and fifth wheel (bi-monthly) k. Lubricate spring locks and stabilizing jacks (bi-monthly). l. Clean contact rings under turntable (bi-monthly). m. Check hydraulic fluid reservoirs (weekly). n. Perform other similar measures as prescribed by manufacturer's manuals and Division policies. (Revised 12/31/15)

604.24 Whenever shop level maintenance is needed or the company commander is unsure of the level of maintenance needed, the Maintenance Shop shall be contacted and the nature of the problem described. At this point, a determination will be made as to whether the needed repairs are classified as routine (minor) or emergency (major). For problems involving apparatus when the nature of the problem is known, the reporting member shall give all pertinent information to the Maintenance Shop supervisor.

604.26 When the status and priority of needed repairs have been determined by authorized personnel, necessary arrangements shall be made to have a mechanic work on the vehicle in quarters, or an appointment shall be set up to have the work done at the Maintenance Shop. All non-emergency or routine (minor) work, such as servicing chief's cars, shall be performed at the shop by appointment. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies

604.28 Any time the Maintenance Shop is contacted to schedule needed repairs or preventive maintenance, and this fact shall be recorded and retained in the apparatus log book. Company commanders and vehicle drivers shall be responsible for the proper use of the apparatus log book.

604.30 Whenever maintenance or repair work is being done at the fire station by shop personnel, the driver or other station personnel shall be available to assist the mechanic as needed. When maintenance or repair work is being performed at the Maintenance Shop all personnel shall wait in the designated waiting area unless the mechanic requests the assistance of one or more members.

604.32 After any work has been performed by maintenance personnel, the driver and/or member responsible for the vehicle shall inspect the vehicle against the shop work order. They shall ensure that the vehicle is adequately repaired and ready for service.
604.34 When necessary, the inspection mentioned in the above paragraph shall include a performance or road test in the maintenance shop area or other convenient location.

604.35 Upon completion of repair or maintenance work, appropriate entries shall be made in the Apparatus Log concerning the work that was performed and any other pertinent information regarding the status of the vehicle. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies

604.36 Regularly scheduled oil changes, filter replacements, and general chassis lubrication of all Division vehicles shall be performed according to the following schedule: Diesel Powered Apparatus: Oil and Filter Change..................... 100 hours Fuel Filter Change.......................... as needed Lubrication....................................... monthly NOTE: For those diesel engines not equipped with engine-hour meters, the odometer reading shall be used, converting each 4000 engine miles to 100 engine hours. Gasoline Powered Apparatus: Oil and Filter Change.......... 4,000 road miles Lubrication..................................................... According to manufacturer’s recommendation -usually with the oil change

604.38 Specialized vehicles may require additional routine or preventive maintenance care at the station level according to the particular requirements established for such vehicles. Company commanders shall ensure that the required care and maintenance activities are provided for any specialized vehicles under their supervision.

604.40 Vehicle engine temperatures should be maintained within the range of 160 to 190 degrees F for gasoline fueled engines, and within the range of 190 to 212 degrees F for diesel powered engines. If these optimum temperatures cannot be maintained, either by using the auxiliary cooler or radiator fill valve, the Maintenance Shop shall be notified.
604.42 (Deleted 12/31/15) Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies

604.44 On-duty company commanders and bureau heads shall ensure that, on the 20th day of each month, the information necessary to accurately compile the monthly mileage report is obtained for each vehicle permanently assigned to their station, including supplementary apparatus.

604.46 Fuel credit cards used by the Division of Fire are issued through Fleet Management and are to be used for the purchase of either gasoline or diesel fuel. Other needed items or services shall be provided by the Maintenance Shop.

604.47 Whenever possible, the following priorities shall be adhered to when deciding where to obtain fuel: 1. Division of Fire fuel tanks 2. Fleet Management service station at Groves Road 3. Fleet fuel card facilities – self-service only Consideration should be given to the number of miles that must be traveled to obtain fuel. Self-service pumps should always be used. Diesel powered apparatus should be fueled from the fire station fuel tanks whenever possible. (Revised 12/31/15)
604.48 (Deleted 12/31/15) OUT-OF-TOWN VEHICLE REPAIRS

604.50 When vehicle repairs are required on a Division vehicle being used by a member traveling out-of-town, the member must pay for the repairs with his or her own funds. The member will be reimbursed for the cost of the repairs after returning to the City and submitting the appropriate documentation through the chain of command. The documentation should include a memo to the Chief, explaining the circumstances in detail and requesting reimbursement. The memo should be attached to a paid receipt showing the cost of the repairs. For the purposes of this policy, “out-of-town” is defined as any area outside of Franklin County and the counties immediately adjacent to Franklin County. Members traveling out-of-town in Division vehicles are expected to understand this policy before traveling. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies SUPPLEMENTARY APPARATUS - MAINTENANCE AND PROCEDURES

606.00 The supplementary apparatus of the Division of Fire serves two very important functions: initially, this apparatus must be available for use as replacement apparatus when the regular first-line apparatus is out of service; in addition, this apparatus must be maintained in a constant state of readiness for use in the event of large scale fire or other disaster.
606.02 Supplementary apparatus may be used either as a substitute for regularly assigned apparatus or as an additional resource to be used by call-in personnel.

606.04 It is essential that all supplementary apparatus receive proper care and maintenance and be fully outfitted with a full complement of tools and equipment. Station Captains and other officers in charge of the various units shall, under the supervision of their Battalion Chief, ensure that all supplementary apparatus assigned to their respective stations is continually checked and maintained.
606.06 An equipment check will be performed on all supplementary apparatus daily. This is the responsibility of personnel assigned to the station or bureau to which such apparatus is assigned.

606.08 There shall be three (3) equipment lists maintained for each piece of supplementary apparatus. One shall be kept on the apparatus, one shall be kept on file at the station or bureau to which the apparatus is assigned, and an informational copy shall be maintained on file at the Tools and Equipment Office.

606.10 Any requests for changes in the complement of equipment carried on the supplementary apparatus shall be forwarded through channels to the Support Services Bureau Head. Information concerning any approved changes shall be made available to all personnel, and equipment lists will then be revised as necessary. (Revised 12/31/15) Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies

606.12 Motors on supplementary apparatus shall be started and run for thirty (30) minutes each week. The Station Captain should establish a regularly scheduled time for this requirement. The pressure governor or relief valve of supplementary engines should be tested at this time. (Revised 12/31/15)

606.16 The Fire Maintenance Liaison Office (FMLO) shall maintain an up-to-date list of each piece of supplementary apparatus and its location. Whenever any supplementary apparatus is put into service, either as first-line or extra apparatus, and whenever such apparatus is moved from its regularly assigned location to another station, office, bureau, or shop for any reason, the FMLO and Company Commander at the regularly assigned location shall be notified of such action immediately. The FMLO shall also be notified when the apparatus is returned to its regularly assigned location. For example: Repairs to E-1 are complete and following change-over, the crew delivers the supplementary apparatus XE-18 to Fleet Maintenance. The FMLO and Station 18 shall be notified. (Revised 12/31/15)

606.18 Station Captains shall prepare and maintain apparatus log book for each piece of supplementary apparatus assigned to their care. These apparatus log books will be uniform throughout the Division and may be ordered from the Supply Section. The vehicle brass tag number and any other particular identifying number shall be placed on the front cover of the log book.

606.20 The supplementary apparatus log book shall be divided into three main sections as listed below, and shall include information pertinent to each section as is explained in the following paragraphs. The three sections are: (1) Log Section, (2) Hose Section, and (3) Maintenance Section. (Revised 12/31/15) Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies Also listed in the Log Section will be any information or data pertinent to the movement or reassignment of the apparatus, regardless of whether such movement is of a permanent or temporary nature. Anytime supplementary apparatus is placed in

606.22 All entries placed in any section of the log book will list the following information: (1) the date of each entry (left hand column), (2) sufficient information to explain each entry, and (3) the station or bureau, unit, rank, and signature of the person making each entry. (Revised 12/31/15)

606.24 Officers or other members who neglect to properly complete the required entries in the supplementary apparatus log book will be held accountable for any subsequently discovered discrepancies. (Revised 12/31/15) SUPPLEMENTARY APPARATUS - LOG SECTION

606.26 Any information relative to movement of apparatus or status of equipment should be listed in this section. The daily equipment check shall be listed, recording the date, name of person making check, and list of any equipment missing or in need of replacement. If there is no equipment missing, this fact shall be stated in the entry. Whenever it is found that there is any equipment missing, and such equipment has not been listed as missing on previous entries, an attempt to locate the missing equipment shall be made by the person noticing the shortage. If the missing equipment cannot be located, the Station Captain, or his alternate, who is responsible for the apparatus shall be notified. This officer shall complete and submit Form ET-68, "Report of Equipment. Lost" and shall also initiate a request for replacement of the items or items involved by sending an Intra-Divisional Communication through the normal channels of communication to the supply office. Included with the information required to be listed on Form ET-68 shall be the name and rank of the last person to sign the record book prior to the discovery that the equipment was missing. This member shall be held responsible for the missing equipment and, if neglect or misuse is indicated, may be subject to disciplinary measures. 606.28 Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies service or is moved or reassigned from its regular station or bureau, the officer or other Division member assuming responsibility for such apparatus shall check the present complement of equipment against the authorized equipment list and make the appropriate entry in the log book. Another complete equipment check shall be performed when the apparatus is returned to its regularly assigned location. (Revised 12/31/15) SUPPLEMENTARY APPARATUS - HOSE SECTION

606.30 All hose permanently assigned to the supplementary apparatus shall be listed in alphabetical and numerical order, beginning with the largest hose, as listed on Hose Form EL-66. Hose sent into the shop to be repaired, replaced, condemned, etc., shall be listed both in the record book and in the back of the company journal on Form EL-66. The "Hose Load Card", Form EI-52, shall be prepared in duplicate and properly revised each time that the sequence of the hose on the apparatus is changed. One copy of this form shall be kept in a prominent location on the apparatus for use by the pump operator, and the duplicate copy shall be kept in the apparatus log book.

606.32 Hose assigned to supplementary apparatus should be properly marked and should be kept separate from the regular hose inventory carried at the station to which the apparatus is permanently or temporarily assigned. If it becomes necessary to use hose from the station inventory to complete the required hose load on a piece of supplementary apparatus, such hose shall be removed from the apparatus when it is reassigned to another station or location. SUPPLEMENTARY APPARATUS - MAINTENANCE SECTION

606.34 All maintenance work and repairs, whether major or minor in nature, shall be recorded in the Maintenance Section of the log book. This shall include a listing of all oil changes, lubrications, etc., together with mileage information and any other data which may be needed to properly complete related periodic reports. Proper signatures will be entered as necessary, either by the officer responsible for having any minor repairs or routine maintenance performed, or by maintenance personnel completing any major repairs. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies At the beginning of each shift, immediately after roll call, company members shall check all tools and equipment for presence, cleanliness, and ability to perform the functions intended.

606.36 Whenever any supplementary apparatus is assigned to locations such as the Training Academy or Logistics Center, the Division member delivering the apparatus shall conduct a thorough equipment check immediately prior to releasing the vehicle to the jurisdiction of the bureau involved. Any missing or damaged tools or equipment will be properly recorded in the vehicle log book at this time. Another thorough check will be made when the apparatus is picked up from such bureau by the Division member picking it up, and any shortages will be noted and reported through channels to the Chief.

606.38 Members charged with the security of the bureau or office to which apparatus has been delivered shall be required to take those precautions necessary to ensure that the hose, tools, and other equipment assigned to such apparatus is safeguarded.

606.40 When supplementary apparatus is to be taken or sent to the shop to undergo repairs, and it is expected that it will remain there for a period of time exceeding 24 hours, all equipment assigned to such apparatus including hose fittings, shall be removed from the apparatus and kept at the station to which it is assigned. Only the log book of the vehicle being repaired will remain with the apparatus. (Revised 12/31/15)

606.48 Company Commanders shall be responsible for ensuring that all apparatus assigned to a particular station or bureau, temporarily assigned to another station or bureau is returned to its permanent place of storage in a clean, well maintained condition. All hose, ladders, tools, equipment, and any other items assigned to such vehicles or apparatus shall be intact and properly accounted for. TOOLS AND EQUIPMENT - MAINTENANCE AND PROCEDURES

606.18 Whenever possible, respiratory protective systems will be returned to a condition of operational readiness (cylinders changed, facepieces cleaned, etc.) before leaving the fire or emergency scene to return to quarters.

608.00 General maintenance of tools and equipment assigned to the various companies of the Division shall be performed by company members under the direction of the Company Commander. 608.02 Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies

608.04 During this equipment check, special attention should be given those tools that are used infrequently and therefore do not receive the constant check of use. Members should also take note of any improper storage practices, and make the necessary corrections at this time.

608.06 After completing the daily equipment check, appropriate entries shall be made in the company journal with regard to the status of the equipment. Missing or damaged tools or equipment shall be listed, and any other pertinent information concerning such equipment shall be recorded and, if necessary, appropriate reports submitted. The failure or damage of tools, equipment, or hose requires that a letter of explanation be initiated by the Company Commander and sent through the proper channels to the Chief.
608.08 If there are no missing items, an appropriate notation to this effect shall be entered in the company journal.

608.10 Before leaving the scene of a fire or other emergency where any tools or other items of equipment were either used or removed from the apparatus, a complete check of the equipment shall be made. If possible, any missing equipment will be located before returning to quarters.

608.12 As soon as practical after returning to quarters, all equipment shall be returned to a state of operational readiness. Particular attention shall be given to the respiratory protective breathing apparatus systems, to ensure that such equipment is ready to be used in subsequent emergency situations.

608.16 It is the policy of the Division of Fire that all respiratory protective breathing apparatus systems be thoroughly checked and cleaned daily and after each use. These systems must be handled carefully; when removed after use at a fire or emergency scene, they shall be returned to their proper places on the apparatus - not thrown or placed on the ground or in a corner. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies

608.20 Tools or other items of equipment not meeting firefighting standards, whether found to be in such condition during the course of a routine equipment check or determined by any other means, shall be either, cleaned, lubricated, or repaired as necessary. If conditions warrant they shall be tagged and sent to Tools and Equipment for repair or replacement.

608.22 All gasoline powered tools and equipment shall be started and run outdoors weekly until the individual piece of equipment reaches its operating temperature. This should normally be accomplished within ten to twenty minutes. Equipment such as generators, saws, exhaust fans, electrical cords, etc., shall be maintained according to the specific requirements of each piece of equipment. (Revised 12/31/15)
608.24 Nozzles should be checked frequently and should be handled carefully. Nozzles are precision instruments and should not be dropped, dragged, or otherwise mishandled. (Revised 12/31/15)
608.26 Ladders shall be inspected regularly and after each use.

608.28 Ropes shall be protected from moisture and shall not be stored with sharp tools or objects. Ropes shall be checked after each use, and a thorough inspection of all ropes shall be performed every six months, as is further explained in Section 618.00 of this manual. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies

608.30 In general, maintenance rules for all Division tools and equipment are as follows: 1. Maintain vehicle or individual brass tag number and readily visible company identification numbers on each tool or item of equipment. 2. Keep all unpainted surfaces free of rust. 3. Keep all moving parts lightly oiled. 4. Clean and repaint appropriate tools when necessary. 5. Keep chromed tools free of dirt and grease. 6. Attempt to use the proper tool or item of equipment for the task to be performed. POWER TOOLS AND EQUIPMENT - MAINTENANCE AND PROCEDURES

610.00 The power tools and equipment used in the Division of Fire today are complicated, expensive, and easily damaged. Constant care and maintenance is required to keep these tools ready for effective use.

610.02 Proper storage of power tools on the apparatus is of prime importance. Company officers and other Division members assigned to be in charge of Division apparatus shall ensure that all power tools are stored securely in their proper compartments.

610.04 All members shall be familiar with the use and operation of all power tools carried on the apparatus assigned to their station including rescue companies. Many specialized tools require more knowledge and skill to operate than do most standard tools carried on engine and ladder companies.

610.06 Power tools requiring weekly scheduled tests and preventive maintenance operations which are performed at the station level shall normally be scheduled for such tests and operations on Monday. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies BOATS, BOAT MOTORS AND EQUIPMENT MAINTENANCE AND PROCEDURES
612.00 The following procedure has been established to ensure that all boats, motors, and items of water rescue equipment are maintained in a state of readiness.
612.02 The responsibility for maintaining the boats and equipment will be that of the station to which they are assigned.
612.04 Each boat will be assigned a log book which will consist of an equipment list, tool and equipment status (RL-135), weekly check forms, and a record of maintenance.

612.06 All equipment checks and motor run tests will be performed on Wednesday of each week by the personnel assigned at the responsible station. Personnel shall check the condition of the trailer, the trailer tires, and proper inflation of the inflatable boats.

612.10 When boat, trailer, or equipment is found to be in need of repair, Tools and Equipment shall be notified. If repairs are to be made to the motor, Tools and Equipment will make the necessary arrangements to have the motor repaired. (Revised 12/31/15)
612.12 If any equipment is missing or damaged, the appropriate entries shall be made on the Boat Log and an ET-68 completed if necessary.
612.14 The Station Captain shall periodically review the boat log to ensure that the weekly checks are being conducted and the appropriate log entries are being made. BOAT MOTOR RUN TEST
612.16 Each boat will be assigned a motor flusher as part of its normal equipment. When conducting the Motor Run Test, the flusher MUST BE USED.

612.18 Thoroughly wet the lower unit of the motor and the rubber cubs on the flusher. Slide the flusher in place over the water intake openings. Fasten a garden hose to the flusher connector and turn water on far enough to assure proper cooling. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies
612.20 Place the motor in neutral and start. Run the motor at SHIFT SPEED for five (5) minutes.
612.22 DO NOT LEAVE THE MOTOR UNATTENDED WHILE RUNNING. Continuously monitor the discharge and stop engine immediately if little or no water is being emitted.

612.24 Inspect hose for kinking or misalignment of the flusher. Restart motor and continue test. If problem still exists, stop the engine and notify the Tools and Equipment immediately. If it is felt that the boat cannot be used in an emergency situation, the Fire Alarm Office shall also be notified that the boat is out of service. BOAT MOTOR FUEL PROCEDURES AND PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE
612.26 All 2-cycle motors must be run on a gasoline/oil mixture. The oil (lubricant) may be obtained from Tool and Equipment. (Revised 12/31/15)

612.28 Use the proper outboard oil/gasoline mixture as marked on the specific motor. Make certain to follow the directions on the can when mixing. In addition to the oil (lubricant), a gasoline stabilizer shall also be added.

612.30 At no time will gas and oil be mixed in less than 6 gallon quantities. Whenever the tank falls below 1/2 full, the fuel shall be removed and put in an approved container and a new 6 gallons mixed. The fuel that has been removed should be disposed of by putting it in the fuel tank of any vehicle that uses gasoline.
612.32 If the fuel is over 1 year old, it is to be replaced even if the tank is more than half full. Information on fuel changes can be obtained from the boat log weekly check form.

612.34 The lower end of the motor contains grease that must be changed annually. The change, along with a preventive maintenance check, will be performed in April of each year and scheduled by the Maintenance Shop. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies FIRE HOSE - GENERAL
614.00 Fire hose shall not be allowed to remain on the apparatus when in a muddy or otherwise soiled condition. (Revised 12/31/15)

614.04 Hose having jackets constructed of synthetic fibers may pick up contaminants, glass, or other debris at fire or other emergency scenes which may prove to be harmful to apparatus, personnel, or public property if not removed from the hose. (Revised 12/31/15)

614.06 Hose shall be either cleaned or replaced with a clean, dry supply as conditions warrant. All mud and debris shall be removed by washing or brushing and, when necessary, hose shall be dried in accordance with the requirements established for the particular type of hose.

614.08 Under normal conditions hose used at fires, during training evolutions, or for any other purpose will be changed or cleaned as necessary. This shall be done either by members assigned to the work shift that used such hose, or by members working other shifts. In the latter case, it is preferable that the work is accomplished during the morning hours on the shift or unit following that on which the hose was used.

614.10 Whenever hose is changed, this fact and any related information shall be recorded in the Company Journal, both on the finished log and in the Company Record on Form EL-51 (Hose Load Record). The Hose Load Card (EI-52) carried on the apparatus shall also be properly revised each time the hose is changed.

614.12 When the amount of hose to be changed exceeds one half (1/2) of the normal complement of a particular size hose (excluding 2” or smaller), the Fire Alarm Office must be contacted and permission obtained to call the apparatus out of service in order to make the change. If changing less than one half (1/2) of the hose load, companies need not call out of service. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies

614.14 In most instances, when it becomes necessary to change hose the Company Commander shall first cause the proper amount of replacement hose to be laid out on the apparatus floor or other convenient location, with the hose coupled together so as to expedite this task. In any event, when changing hose the used load shall be removed from the apparatus and the fresh supply put in its place as quickly as possible.
614.16 All gaskets in hose connections shall be inspected before hose sections are coupled together and any missing or damaged gaskets shall be replaced before the hose is loaded on the apparatus.
614.20 Extreme cold causes deterioration of rubber. However, fire hose may be stored in cold storage areas if the hose is first thoroughly drained and dried.
614.22 Fire hose is liable to crack if it is bent while in a frozen condition. Care shall be taken to avoid bending frozen fire hose.

614.24 The folds of all hose loaded on Division apparatus shall be changed at least monthly to reduce damage from kinks, mildew, and other harmful actions. The folds of synthetic rubber ribbed hose shall be changed three (3) times per year, in January, May, and September, once by each unit. During the change the hose shall be inspected for damage and the couplings lubricated.
614.26 All hose stored in fire stations shall be removed from its place of storage, unrolled, inverted, and re-rolled at least quarterly. (Revised 12/31/15)

614.30 Under no circumstances shall fire hose be allowed to go longer than one (1) year without having water passed through it. This applies to all hose assigned to and stored in the various stations and bureaus, including both auxiliary or reserve supplies and that hose normally assigned to or loaded on the apparatus. Normally the annual hose test will accomplish this requirement. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies

614.32 All hose stored in the various fire stations shall, whenever possible, be stored so as to permit the free circulation of air and shall be inspected at least monthly for signs of mildew and other indications of deterioration.
614.34 When storing fire hose, care should be taken to see that it is not exposed to sunlight, or to very hot, dry air.
614.36 When fire hose is being used, care shall be taken to see that the section nearest the engine or hydrant is not being chafed by vibration at the point of contact with the ground.

614.38 Acids, oils, rust, gasoline, chemicals, and fumes arising from various processes are injurious to some types of fire hose. Contact with such substances shall be avoided if at all possible. HOSE INVENTORY
614.40 A complete and accurate hose inventory shall be kept in the Company Record on Form EL-66 and the instructions on the back of that form shall be strictly followed.
614.42 At the time of the Annual Hose Test, a duplicate hose inventory, listed on Form EL-66, shall be compiled and forwarded to the Bureau of Support Services.

614.44 Company Officers are responsible for ensuring that hose inventory forms are promptly revised as needed to accurately reflect current hose supplies. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies HOSE REPAIR AND REPLACEMENT

614.46 When hose is sent to the Hose Repair to be repaired, it shall be prepared as follows: (1) (2) (3) (4) Clean and dry each section Attach repair tag stating the date, section number, officer's name, station, unit, brief description of damage, location of damage, and whether the hose does or does not leak. Circle any leaks or other defects with a permanent black marker. List damaged hose number of Form EL-66 in the company log. (Revised 12/31/15)
614.48 Companies in need of replacement hose shall submit a written request through the Chain of Command to Support-7. (Revised 12/31/15)

614.50 Upon receiving the replacement hose, the company officer shall assure that all appropriate information is listed on Form EL-66 in the company log; hose is marked according to Sections 602.16 through 602.22; hose is tested as stated in Section
614.54 Hose will be repaired, if possible and returned to the station from which it came.

614.56 If the hose is damaged beyond repair, Hose Repair will make out an RT-154 (official Intra-Divisional Communication), stating that the hose is either "Unfit for Service" or "Condemned" and forward it to the station from which it came. Station personnel shall make appropriate log entries upon receipt of theRT-154. (Revised 12/31/15) HOSE TEST PROCEDURES

614.58 Each year during the month of May, all fire hose shall be tested by subjecting it to predetermined maximum text pressures. These tests will be conducted by company officers under the general supervision of the Emergency Services Bureau and the results recorded on the hose inventory/test record (EL-66) by the company officers involved. (Revised 12/31/15) Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies

614.64 Prior to the annual hose test, station captains shall be responsible for preparing an accurate, up-to-date list of all fire hose assigned to their stations including hose depot supplies where appropriate, as listed in Section 614.40. Hose shall be listed alphabetically and numerically for each size. Hose found to be defective or unserviceable during the test will be taken back to the fire station and properly prepared for repair or exchange as listed in Section 614.46.

614.66 Test pressure for all hose will be 250 psi with the exception of soft suctions and 5" hose which will be tested at 150 PSI. NOTE: It is established Division policy that pump pressure in excess of 250 PSI shall not be allowed unless specifically authorized by the officer in charge of the fire, or by prior authorization based on particular capacities or requirements of specialized equipment.

614.68 All hose testing shall be based upon procedures contained in NFPA 1962, "SERVICE TESTING OF FIRE HOSE", current edition of NFPA Handbook (with same name), and Division SOP #06-04-03 “Hose Testing Procedures.” (Revised 12/31/15)

614.82 The company officer shall complete the hose records to indicate the condition of each length of hose tested. He/she shall correct the hose load cards and hose records in the Log as necessary to reflect test results.

614.84 Station captains shall be responsible for ensuring that all fire hose assigned to their station is properly tested prior to its being placed in service as a part of the stations regular hose inventory. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies HIGH PRESSURE HOSE

614.90 All high pressure hose used by the Division shall be tested annually by the Hose Repair Technician. These tests shall be coordinated by the Company Officer in-charge of the Division’s Logistics Center and shall conform to the guidelines and applicable sections of NFPA 1962: Standard for the Inspection, Care, & Use of Fire Hose Couplings, Nozzles; and the Service Testing of Fire Hose. (Added 12/31/15)

614.92 The Hose Repair Technician or designee will contact each fire station, verifying the amount of High Pressure Hose assigned. The Technician will then coordinate switching out assigned HP hose for loaner HP hose, one Battalion at a time. Each station will assist the Hose Technician in gathering and rolling up these two 100 ft. sections of 2.5” HP Hose. The turnaround time to test each Battalions HP Hose will be approximately four days. (Added 12/31/15)

614.94 All HP Hose will be properly tested using the Division’s High Pressure Hose Tester. All HP Hose passing the HP Test will be returned to the appropriate stations and switched out with the loaner HP Hose. Any hose not passing the HP Test will be condemned by the Hose Technician and a loaner section of HP hose will be reassigned to replace the condemned hose. (Added 12/31/15)

614.92 These tests will be supervised by the Company Officer in-charge of the Logistics Center under the general supervision of the Support Services Bureau and the results recorded on the Hose Test Record (EL-50). Copies of these records will be submitted to each Company Officer to record these results in their Inventory/Test Records (EL66/EL/50). (Added 12/31/15) Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies SALVAGE COVERS
616.00 Salvage covers may be canvas, vinyl, or disposable plastic sheeting, utilized to reduce damage from fire, smoke, water, heat, cold, or weather during and after a fire. (Added 12/31/15)
616.02 Disposable plastic sheeting is obtained from the Supply Section. (Added 12/31/15)
616.06 - 616.08 (Deleted 12/31/15) ROPES - MAINTENANCE AND PROCEDURES

618.00 Ropes used by the Division of Fire are constructed of either natural fibers or synthetic materials. All ropes shall be cared for and inspected in accordance with the provisions of this section. (Revised 12/31/15)

618.02 Ropes made of natural fibers, such as manila, hemp, should be cleaned by brushing, flaking, or peeling - never by washing or rinsing with water. Ropes constructed of synthetic materials, such as polypropylene may be cleaned by using water and, if necessary, a mild detergent.

618.04 Inspection of all ropes shall be completed during the months of May and November. Station Captains shall see that the Rope Inspection Form is properly completed at the time of these inspections, and that it is then forwarded through channels to Tools and Equipment. (Revised 12/31/15)
618.06 The Tool and Equipment Section shall use the information received on the Rope Inspection Form to schedule any necessary replacements.

618.08 Ropes should not be carried in compartments or other areas where they may become damaged through contact with sharp edged tools or similar surfaces. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies RADIATION INSTRUMENTS - MAINTENANCE AND PROCEDURES

622.00 Radiological Instruments have been assigned to all fire stations and to various vehicles of the Division. These instruments are provided and maintained by the Emergency Management Agency for use in the event of a national emergency, and are also available for Division use in local emergencies or other situations involving radioactive materials. (Revised 12/31/15)

622.06 In order to be certain that this equipment is adequately maintained and will operate properly when needed, all radiation instruments assigned to the Division shall be check and tested by the personnel assigned to the stations or bureaus where such instruments are located. (Revised 12/31/15)

622.08 Radiation instruments that are defective or in need of repair shall be sent to Office Research and Innovation. When sending in these instruments, be sure to include the entire kit and attach a repair tag stating the date, station number, unit, officers name, and instruments that are defective. The Office of Research and Innovation will then forward the kits to the Emergency Management Agency for exchange. (Revised 12/31/15)
622.10 (Deleted 12/31/15) Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies FIRE HYDRANT INSPECTIONS AND PROCEDURES (inserted from 540.00 – 12/31/15)

640.00 Fire Hydrant Use and Operation: On all occasions where fire hydrants are to be used, precautions shall be taken when opening and closing the hydrant valves to see that they are operated slowly. This procedure is necessary in order to prevent a water hammer which could cause damage to water mains and residential service lines. (Revised from 540.00 – 12/31/15)

640.02 Whenever a hydrant is used for any purpose between the dates of October 15 and April 15 of each year, the hydrant shall be pumped dry and this information reported on Water-Web immediately upon returning to quarters. It is also required that this information be listed in the Company Journal. (Revised from 540.02 – 12/31/15)

640.04 When a hydrant is being used and water is leaking or spraying from around the top of stem, it is recommended that the hydrant operating stem be closed approximately one-half of a turn after the hydrant has been fully opened. This procedure may stop the leak. If the leak does not stop, report it on Water-Web upon returning to quarters. (Revised from 540.04 – 12/31/15)

640.06 Illegal Use of Hydrants: No person other than employees of the Division of Fire and/or the Division of Water, operating within the parameters of their respective duties, shall connect any hose to or draw any water from any city fire hydrant without a valid permit approved by the Fire Chief and the Administrator of the Division of Water, or their designees. Any hydrant usage without such permit is a violation of Columbus City Code 2517.04. Hydrant permits may be obtained from the Division of Water Sales Office located at 910 Dublin Road. (Revised from 540.06 – 12/31/15)

640.08 Persons authorized to use fire hydrants shall not violate any conditions of the permit or any of the rules and regulations concerning such permit. Any violation of the conditions or rules and regulations pertaining to a hydrant permit is in direct opposition to Columbus City Code 2577.04. (Revised from 540.08 – 12/31/15) Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies

640.10 All members of the Division of Fire shall report to the Fire Alarm Office any obvious or suspected illegal use of a fire hydrant that they have observed or been notified of. The Fire Alarm Office shall dispatch a fire company to the scene in order to obtain all pertinent information surrounding the incident. This should include, but not necessarily be limited to the following items: 1. Location of involved fire hydrant, date and time of incident. The Engine Company shall attempt to shut down the hydrant in question if it is found to be illegally flowing. 2. Name of individual(s) using the fire hydrant, together with their address, date of birth, social security number and driver’s license number, and also, the name and address of individual’s employer. If met with resistance that may cause injury to personnel or damage to City property, the officer in charge shall withdraw all Division members to the apparatus. 3. Description of any involved vehicle at the scene and license number of same. 4. 5. 6.) Description of any equipment and/or tools used to obtain water from the fire hydrant. Purpose for which the water was obtained, fire hydrant permit number if applicable. Name, badge number, and cruiser number of any police personnel at the scene. If there is immediate danger to personnel the officer shall call for the police on an emergency, request a Battalion Chief to be dispatched to a rendezvous point and be guided by his/her decision. The company officer shall submit, through channels, all of the information obtained to the Division's Hydrant Coordinator at the Fire Prevention Bureau. This bureau shall file the appropriate charges if such action is indicated. These procedures shall also be followed whenever the Division of Police or other concerned persons advise the Fire Alarm Office of any suspected illegal hydrant usage. (Revised from 540.10 – 12/31/15) Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies

640.12 A map (Station and Battalion Water Atlas) showing the locations of all hydrants within assigned districts shall be prepared and maintained by each Company Commander, who shall also ensure that such map is kept updated, both for company schooling purposes and for the possible use by the Battalion Chief. (Revised from 540.12 – 12/31/15)

640.14 When a hydrant district has been inspected and no defects have been found, no written hydrant inspection report will be required. However, if any defective hydrants are encountered, the inspector shall document that information on Water-Web upon return to quarters. (Revised from 540.14 – 12/31/15)

640.16 Whenever a hydrant is reported to have been used for any purpose whatsoever by any municipal department other than the Fire Division between the dates of October 15 and April 15, the Fire Alarm Office shall be notified. The Fire Alarm Office shall enter this information in Water-Web. (Revised from 540.16 – 12/31/15)

640.18 Each year from October 15 to April 15, whenever fire hydrants have been used for any purpose, it shall be the responsibility of the fire company using the hydrant to record such usage on Water-Web These hydrants shall be inspected daily, until each hydrant has been found to be without water on three (3) consecutive days. Any hydrant that continues to leak after the third consecutive daily check shall be reported on Water-Web. (Revised from 540.18 – 12/31/15)

640.20 Whenever a hydrant is found to be leaking between the dates of October 15 and April 15, and leakage cannot be stopped by employing recommended procedures, the hydrant inspector shall record the hydrant on Water-Web. In addition, all hydrants used at any fire scene, emergency incident, or for any other purpose shall be reported on Water-Web for inclusion on the special hydrant list. (Revised from 540.20 – 12/31/15)
640.22 Each shall maintain a current “hydrant-out” list by checking Water-Web daily. (Revised from 540.22 – 12/31/15) Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies

640.24 Company Commanders are responsible for seeing that the pages of each Water Atlas assigned to their station are maintained accurately and kept up to date. This includes any Water Atlas assigned to any vehicle or apparatus quartered therein. (Revised from 540.24 – 12/31/15) Fire Hydrant Inspections

640.26 Inspection of fire hydrants by Division personnel shall be carried out in a systematic manner, with the goal of insuring that all hydrants are accessible, readily visible, and completely operational when it becomes necessary to use them. An additional purpose of these inspections is to familiarize Division personnel with the location of all fire hydrants within the corporate limits of the City of Columbus, including not only municipal hydrants, but private hydrants and various government owned hydrants as well. Company Commanders shall insure that an updated map of the assigned hydrant district is provided to the hydrant inspector. (Revised from 540.26 – 12/31/15)

640.28 When inspecting hydrants, Division members shall pay particular attention to the following listed items: (Any defects found shall be noted on Water-Web). 1.) Missing hydrant caps; outlet threads or caps showing indications of 2.) 3.) 4.) 5.) having been damaged or rusted away. Badly worn hydrant operating nuts, or any indication that the hydrant may have been operated by using a pipe wrench. Any condition noted which might cause a hydrant to be obscured from view or installed in such a way as to render it difficult to put into service. Hydrant outlets which are less than 12 inches above the surrounding ground level, or outlets or domes which extend beyond the curb line. Any condition surrounding or in the vicinity of a hydrant which is liable to cause injury, accident, or property damage. Special attention shall be given to those areas where construction work of some type has recently been performed, and where concrete sidewalks or ramp areas have been damaged or are missing. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies 6.) Water in the hydrant barrel. (If water is found between the dates of October 15th and April 15th, pump the hydrant and report it on Water-Web.) (Revised from 540.28 – 12/31/15)

640.30 Any time an employee of the Division of Fire notes a defect which would render a hydrant unserviceable - such as water frozen in the hydrant, hydrant knocked off or damaged by collision, broken valve stem, damaged outlet threads, damaged operating nut, or any other defect - the hydrant shall immediately reported on Water-Web. (Revised from 540.30 – 12/31/15)

640.34 Each Monday, the Division Hydrant Coordinator shall prepare and distribute a "Hydrant Out of Service" report from Water-Web to the Emergency Services Deputy Chiefs, all Battalion Chiefs, the Water Maintenance Engineer and the Water Distribution Manager. This report will show all known public hydrants within the City of Columbus that are currently out of service. (Revised from 540.34 – 12/31/15)
640.38 Company Commanders shall be responsible for ensuring that the "Hydrant Out-of-Service List" is kept up to date on a daily basis. (Revised from 540.38 – 12/31/15)

640.40 Company Commanders shall be responsible for ensuring that missing fire hydrant caps within their respective hydrant inspection districts are replaced as necessary. In addition, whenever hydrant caps are found to be missing from hydrants in a given company's first-in response area, they should be replaced as needed. Replacement hydrant caps may be obtained from Supply, using regular requisition procedures. If replacement caps are unavailable at any given time, a record shall be kept of hydrants needing replacement caps, and replacements made when caps are obtained. The Supply Office shall notify the Division Hydrant Coordinator whenever replacement caps need to be restocked. (Revised from 540.40 – 12/31/15) Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VI Division Maintenance Policies

640.42 Whenever a missing hydrant cap is replaced, the Division member replacing the cap shall first flush the hydrant. This procedure is necessary to check if foreign objects or materials are within the hydrant barrel. As always, whenever a hydrant is flushed between the dates of October 15 and April 15, the hydrant shall then be pumped and reported on Water-Web for the special hydrant three-day check. (Revised from 540.42 – 12/31/15)
640.44 Whenever hydrant caps are placed on hydrants they are to be made snug by using a hydrant wrench, to minimize unauthorized removal of caps by hand. (Revised from 540.44 – 12/31/15)

640.46 Company Commanders shall be responsible for the care and inspection of the fire hydrant closest to their respective stations, as this hydrant is normally used for training purposes. (Revised from 540.46 – 12/31/15)

640.48 Division members must be aware that some privately owned fire hydrants and certain hydrants belonging to other municipalities have 5-sided (pentagonal shaped) operating nuts which require tools other than the Division's standard hydrant wrench to operate. (Revised from 540.48 – 12/31/15)

640.50 Members must realize that certain hydrants installed by federal, state, and county governments - as well as some privately owned hydrants - open in a counter-clockwise direction. This, of course, is the direct opposite of the fire hydrants belonging to the City of Columbus, which are opened in a clockwise direction. Members shall always exercise due caution when operating unfamiliar hydrants. (Revised from 540.50 – 12/31/15)

640.52 Members must know that some privately owned hydrants are supplied by fire pumps, and can develop working pressures of 150 psi. or greater. Extreme caution shall be exercised when attempting to operate these hydrants. The water supply to these hydrants may come from public mains, storage tanks, or ponds. (Revised from 540.52 – 12/31/15) Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies

640.54 Members must know that certain hydrants within the corporate limits and surrounding areas of the city have 4 1/2 - inch steamer outlets, requiring utilization of a 4 1/2 to 4-inch reducer before they can be used by the Columbus Division of Fire. (Revised from 540.54 – 12/31/15) Summer Hydrant Inspections

640.56 From April 15 to October 15 of each year, Company Commanders shall require that regular inspections of all city fire hydrants in their assigned districts be conducted. These summer hydrant inspections shall be made on the specific day assigned for this purpose, but may be conducted more frequently if deemed to be necessary. Before engaging in any hydrant inspection activities on days other than those regularly assigned, the appropriate Battalion Chief shall be consulted. (Revised from 540.56 – 12/31/15)

640.58 In addition to inspecting for the items listed in Section 540.28, members conducting summer hydrant inspections shall make certain that all hydrants are readily visible from all directions at all times. They shall cut weeds surrounding any hydrant. If necessary the company officer may contact property owners to trim bushes and/or other vegetation which may be obstructing the hydrant's visibility or accessibility. (Revised from 540.58 – 12/31/15) Winter Hydrant Inspections

640.60 It shall be the duty of the Emergency Services Deputy Chiefs to cause all hydrants within the corporate limits of the City of Columbus to be pumped free of water each fall, prior to the 15th of October, or earlier if weather conditions warrant. Between the dates of October 15 and April 15 of each year, Company Commanders and Acting Officer shall require that all hydrants in their respective assigned districts are inspected on the day designated. If sufficient staffing is not available, the entire company must go on the inspection. If for any reason a hydrant district is not inspected or completed on the assigned day the Company Commander shall log this fact and the hydrant district shall be inspected or completed on the next duty day. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies These winter inspections shall be made in order to determine the condition of each hydrant, and to be certain that all hydrants are pumped free of water above the valve so as to guard against freezing. In the event of heavy snow or unusual icing conditions, additional inspections may be required in order to ensure hydrant operation and visibility. (Revised from 540.60 – 12/31/15)

640.62 When pumping hydrants free of water in preparation for the winter season, the valve stems of hydrants that are not leaking shall not be disturbed; if the hydrant stem is tightened down, the valve seat may be changed and in many cases this action will cause hydrants to start leaking. (Revised from 540.62 – 12/31/15)

640.64 Company Commanders will be responsible for seeing that all known leaking hydrants in their respective hydrant districts are checked each duty day if necessary during freezing weather. (Revised from 540.64 – 12/31/15) Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies Fire Hydrant Flushing Procedures

640.66 Flushing of all city fire hydrants will be accomplished according to the provisions of this section. Division Bulletins containing supplemental information will be published as necessary prior to the time that hydrants are to be flushed. In addition, hydrant flushing activities will be publicized via the news media, stating times, dates, and specific areas of the city that will be involved. (Revised from 540.66 – 12/31/15)

640.68 Hydrant flushing will begin as near to April 15 of each year as possible, and all city hydrants shall be flushed and pumped by October 15 of each year. Whenever possible flush two or three hydrants at one time, so as to avoid a possible water hammer when closing the hydrants. At no time shall more than three hydrants in any given area be flushed at once. (Revised from 540.68 – 12/31/15)

640.70 The flushing of fire hydrants accomplishes several things: it is a positive check, establishing that the hydrant has been turned on at the watch valve; it confirms that the hydrant has worked at least once; it removes foreign objects from the hydrant barrel - such as those placed there by children or vandals; and, it also ejects gravel and similar materials which from time to time are accidentally introduced into the water mains. (Revised from 540.70 – 12/31/15)

640.72 Division members flushing hydrants are cautioned to give due consideration to possible detrimental effects which may result from such procedures. Care should be taken to ensure that vehicle and/or pedestrian traffic is not unnecessarily affected, and that road way shoulders, berms, lawns and other property items are not damaged as a result of the hydrant flushing procedures. (Revised from 540.72 – 12/31/15)

640.74 The soft flush method shall be strictly observed, Company Commanders shall be responsible for insuring that proper hydrant flushing procedures are followed by all members of their respective companies. (Revised from 540.74 – 12/31/15) Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies

640.76 Prior to conducting hydrant flushing operations, Company Commanders shall advise their Battalion Chief of the number of double-handled hydrant wrenches that they will need. This information shall be relayed through proper channels to the Maintenance Section. (Revised from 540.76 – 12/31/15)

640.78 Ordinarily, hydrant flushing operations will be conducted seven (7) days per week between the hours of 0800 and 1700. Each day that hydrant flushing activities are to be conducted, the involved Company Commanders shall notify the appropriate personnel as listed in current Division Bulletins. (Revised from 540.78 – 12/31/15)

640.80 Whenever possible hydrant flushing operations will be conducted in two non-adjoining areas of the city simultaneously, and shall not be conducted in other areas until both have been completed. (Revised from 540.80 – 12/31/15)

640.82 Hydrants which are found to be out of service during the course of flushing operations are to be reported on Water-Web upon returning to quarters. Broken hydrants that are flowing or causing hazardous conditions are to be reported to the Fire Alarm Office as soon as possible, utilizing radio communication. The Fire Alarm Office will then relay all pertinent information regarding such hydrants to the Water Shop. Hydrants that are found to be in need of repair shall also be reported on Water-Web. (Revised from 540.82 – 12/31/15)

640.84 Each day at the completion of hydrant flushing operations, the hydrant maintenance log shall be updated to accurately describe the area that was flushed that day, and the numerical designation of the hydrant district. (Revised from 540.84 – 12/31/15) Hydrant Flushing - Soft Method

640.86 First, remove the four inch (4") hydrant cap. Place a double-handled hydrant wrench on the valve stem. Next, turn the hydrant on slowly using both hands - one hand on each side of the wrench. The hydrant is to be opened until the flow of water from the outlet is no more than two (2) to three (3) feet in front of the hydrant. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies (Note: If one person is unable to turn the hydrant on by following these procedures, the hydrant shall be called out of service on Water-Web.) (Revised from 540.86 – 12/31/15)

640.88 After the hydrant has been flushed sufficiently (the water flowing from the outlet will be clear or almost clear), begin reducing the flow by SLOWLY shutting the hydrant off, again using both hands. Continue closing the hydrant valve slowly until only residual water in the barrel of the hydrant is coming from the outlet. When water ceases to flow from the outlet, splash some of the residual water from the hydrant barrel. If water still continues to flow - however slightly - from the outlet, attempt to stop the flow by slowly and carefully continuing to close the hydrant valve. Do not over tighten the valve stem, as this may damage the valve seat or stem coupling. Hydrants that cannot be completely shut off are to be reported on WaterWeb. Finally, replace the hydrant cap and slightly tighten same with the hydrant wrench to prevent unauthorized removal by hand. (Revised from 540.88 – 12/31/15)

640.90 If the water being flushed from a hydrant does not clear up after having flowed for approximately ten (10) minutes, allow the hydrant to continue flowing. During the course of the day, return and check the hydrant from time to time. If the water has cleared up, close the hydrant. If the water has not cleared up by the conclusion of flushing activities for the day, close the hydrant and notify the Fire Alarm Office of the situation. The FAO will then notify the Water Shop. Complaints of rusty or discolored water are to be referred to the Water Quality Assurance Laboratory. (Revised from 540.90 – 12/31/15)

640.92 If any hydrant should have the valve stem slam shut, or if any hydrant should fail to flow after having been opened six (6) turns, call the hydrant out of service after returning to quarters on Water-Web. If it is believed that an underground leak has been caused by a valve slamming shut, notify to the Fire Alarm Office immediately. They will notify the Water Shop of the leak. If any foreign substance is thought to be in a hydrant barrel and not dislodged by a soft flush, report this fact on the Water-Web. The Water Shop will remove the object. (Revised from 540.92 – 12/31/15) Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter V I Division Maintenance Policies Assignment of Hydrant Districts

640.94 Hydrant districts will be assigned to the various Companies. Districts will be rotated or reassigned as necessary on or about April 15 of each year. Each company’s assigned hydrant district will be rotated 1 Unit to 2 Unit, 2 Unit to 3 Unit, and 3 Unit to 1 Unit. The Station Captain will ensure that the hydrant districts are rotated accurately. (Revised from 540.94 – 12/31/15)

640.96 A master hydrant map will be maintained in each Fire Station; if any boundary of an assigned company district is not understood, the Company Commander responsible for such district shall contact the Division Hydrant Coordinator for clarification. (Revised from 540.96 – 12/31/15)

640.98 All future annexed territories shall be included in and made a part of the existing hydrant districts that they adjoin. All new city hydrant installations shall also be included within the existing districts, but if such installations are not within existing hydrant districts, they too shall be made a part of the hydrant districts that they adjoin. (Revised from 540.98 – 12/31/15) 640.100 (Deleted 12/31/15) 640.102 (Deleted 12/31/15) Private Hydrant Procedures 640.106 Government institutions, private plants, apartment complexes and all other occupancies having their own private fire hydrant system are responsible for maintaining, servicing, pumping, and inspecting such hydrants on a regular basis. (Revised from 540.106 – 12/31/15) 640.108 Battalion Chiefs shall be aware of the following procedures concerning all government or private hydrants within the boundaries of the city hydrant districts assigned to the companies under their supervision. Information explaining proper hydrant maintenance and inspection procedures shall be included with each notification.
