704.00 All employees of the Division of Fire shall be paid on a bi-weekly basis. Payday will be the Thursday immediately following the completion of each designated pay period.
704.02 - 704.14 (Deleted 12/31/15) CALL-IN AND OVERTIME PROCEDURES
706.00 The call-in and overtime procedures of the Division of Fire shall conform to the provisions of this section and to applicable sections of the current master salary ordinance. CALL-IN

706.02 When authorized by the proper authority, and notified by the Chief or designated alternate, the Fire Alarm Office will initiate the call-in of off-duty personnel. The call-in procedures is divided into three classes: Class I or "special" call-in, Class II or "regular" call-in, and Class III or "general" call-in.

706.04 The proper authority for initiating a call-in of off-duty personnel is as follows: Class I (“special” call-in) – Fire Chief Class II (“regular” call-in) – Director of Public Safety Class III (“general” call-in) – Mayor

706.06 CLASS I OR "SPECIAL" CALL-IN: Selected officers and members are called in according to need. This could be based on a predetermined plan where individual expertise and/or special skills are required (i.e., tank specialists, bomb squad, etc.). 706.08 Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures
706.10 CLASS III OR "GENERAL" CALL-IN: All off-duty personnel are called in. Members will be instructed to report to special designated areas, or to their normal duty stations.
706.12 Whenever any of the previously listed call-in procedures are implemented all bureau heads shall be notified.

706.14 In the event of a Class II or a Class III call-in, all Fire Prevention Bureau personnel, Training Section personnel and Maintenance Section personnel shall be included in the call-in, unless orders to the contrary are received. Administration Bureau personnel shall be called in as determined by the manager of that bureau.

706.16 After being authorized by the Chief or designated alternate, the Fire Alarm Office will initiate the appropriate call-in procedure by notifying all off-duty Bureau Chiefs and Battalion Chiefs, according to need as determined by the class of call-in instituted. These chief officers will then contact their company officers or other subordinates who, in turn, will notify the members under their command. All Bureau and Division Officers and their alternates shall maintain an updated call-in list for this purpose.
706.18 All uniformed members that are called in and may be assigned duties requiring protective clothing shall report with their full complement of fire clothing.
706.20 It shall be the policy of the city to avoid overtime work except on the advanced authorization of the Safety Director or in an emergency situation.
706.22 All Division members up to and including the rank of Battalion Chief are eligible to receive overtime pay at the rate of time and one-half the hourly rate.

706.24 Members assigned to 40-hour positions, including those having work schedules of five eight-hour days or four ten-hour days, shall receive overtime pay for all time that they are required to work in excess of that stipulated as their regular daily shift -- or in excess of 40 hours in any week. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures
706.26 Form PT-14 (Report of Overtime Worked) shall be completed and forwarded to the Chief whenever overtime is worked. TRADING OF TIME POLICY
708.00 The trading of time between Division members working different duty shifts may be permitted in keeping with the provisions of this section.

708.02 While it is the policy of the Division to encourage a positive attitude toward approving trades, it must be understood that the trading of time is a privilege - not a right - and may be granted at the discretion of the respective Battalion Chiefs.

708.03 Trading of time by definition does not include payment, either in cash or bartered services, for work. Paying division members to work a partial shift, full shift or multiple shifts for another member is expressly prohibited.

708.04 Recommendations regarding approval or disapproval of trade requests involving their subordinates may be expressed by company commanders or other immediate supervisors. Battalion Chiefs shall carefully weigh the recommendations of a member's immediate supervisor in determining the advisability of granting trade requests.

708.06 (Deleted 12/31/15) 708.08 708.10 Members requesting trades shall insure the appropriate entries are performed in TeleStaff using the most current approved procedure. Failure to follow the designated procedure may result in denial of the trade request. The Battalion Chief of the person requesting the trade is responsible to insure proper TeleStaff procedures are followed. Any disapproval of a trade request will be promptly acknowledged, and accompanied by a written explanation to the employee requesting the trade, detailing the reason for such disapproval. In addition, a memo will be sent to the Fire Chief, explaining the actions taken. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures

708.12 Trades shall ordinarily be between Division members of equal rank, and whenever possible, similar skill levels. However, trades between company commanders, whether Captains or Lieutenants, will usually be permitted during daylight hours. No trades will be permitted that would result in a member of a lower rank working for a higher ranking member between the hours of 2000 to 0800.

708.16 Receiving trades or working trades for more than ten (10) complete tours of duty, or the total hourly equivalent of same in any calendar year, shall not be allowed except by permission of the Chief of the Division. TeleStaff will record all trade dates and times.
708.18 Trades involving a period of time in excess of three (3) consecutive 24-hour shifts shall not be authorized except by permission of the Chief of the Division.

708.20 Members owing time to other Division members as a result of trades must expect to repay this obligation within a reasonable time. Therefore, it is the policy of the Division that, if 180 days have passed since a trade was taken and no request for repayment of the time owed has been tendered, the obligation of the member owing the time shall automatically cease.
708.22 Members working and/or repaying trades shall be limited to not more than 48- consecutive hours-on-duty, including their own regularly scheduled work shift and/ or any overtime work shifts.

708.24 Division members requesting time off by the process of arranging trades shall be held responsible for the period of time in question. For this reason, whenever a Division member fails to report for duty after having agreed to work for another member as per time trade arrangements detailed in this section -- whether for reasons of sickness, emergency, or any other situation -- the Division member originally scheduled to work (the person requesting the trade) shall be obligated to repay the time involved in a manner determined by the Fire Chief. The Division member originally scheduled to work the time will be charged with vacation to the extent he/she has a sufficient Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures balance. The vacation balance available will be utilized and the remainder of time will be charged as leave without pay (LWOP).
708.26 Employees who have agreed to work a trade with another employee shall not be eligible for vacation on the date of the trade.

708.28 Employees who have been scheduled to attend a Division training session shall not be eligible for a trade on the date of the scheduled training, unless the trade had been scheduled before the date on which the training schedule was published.

708.30 Division members who agree to work a trade of twenty-four (24) hours and fail to report for duty for the entire twenty-four (24) hours shall, in addition to the disciplinary hearing before the Fire Chief, will be barred from obtaining a trade for one (1) year.

708.32 Division members who agree to a trade of time and are late in reporting to duty shall be barred from any time trades in the following increments: 60 days 180 days First Late: Second Late: Third Late: 1 year
708.34 Members may work a trade on their Kelly Day. LATE FOR DUTY

710.00 Company Officers and/or other Division supervisors who are responsible for verifying that all Division members under their command are on time when reporting for duty, shall be held strictly accountable for the fair and consistent application of the late policies contained in this section, and shall make no exceptions when recognizing and reporting any deviations from these policies. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures

710.02 Division members who are not physically present at their permanently assigned duty station or properly sanctioned temporary work location and in compliance with the Division grooming code shall be marked as reporting late for duty.

710.04 Members working the three platoon system who are required to stand a formal roll call shall be in formation at 0800 hours and in compliance with 710.02 or be considered late for duty. Members working the three platoon system who are not required to stand a formal roll call with a reporting time of 0700 are required to be in compliance with 710.02 or be considered late for duty. Members working a forty (40) hour work week are required to report to duty at their specified time and be in compliance with 710.02 or be considered late for duty.

710.06 When a member is late in reporting for duty, the Company Commander or other immediate supervisor shall make a verbal report to the appropriate Battalion Chief as soon as reasonably possible, and shall require the member who is late to complete a Late For Duty Report, Form PT-20, including an explanation of why the late occurred. This procedure shall be mandatory.

710.08 Whenever possible, the immediate supervisor shall conduct an investigation of the member's excuse for being late. Comments pertaining to the results of this investigation, together with any other information that the supervisor wishes to present, shall be listed on Form PT-20.
710.10 The Late for Duty Report (Form PT-20) shall be forwarded through proper channels to the Administrative Officer on the same day that the late occurs. (Revised 12/31/15)

710.12 Company Commanders and/or other immediate supervisor shall make the appropriate entries concerning members reporting late for duty on the daily Personnel Status Report (OF-237), the daily log, and in the company journal (Form PL-7). All entries in the company journal less than one (1) year old shall be preserved. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures

710.14 The Battalion Chief or office supervisor receiving the Late For Duty Report through channels shall make any necessary recommendations and reasons for same in the space provided, sign the report, and forward it to the Deputy Chief or appropriate bureau head.

710.16 The Deputy Chief or bureau head receiving the Late For Duty Report will add any necessary recommendations - and the reasons for same - in the space provided, sign the report, and forward the report through channels to the Administrative Officer. (Revised 12/31/15)

710.18 The Administrative Officer, with the Fire Chief's approval, will make the final determination concerning the late, based on the consistently applied criteria listed in Sections 710.20 and 710.22. Only in highly unusual and exceptional situations will a late be excused. (Revised 12/31/15) PENALTIES

710.20 Personnel who are late in reporting for duty will be charged one-tenth (1/10) of an hours pay at their current pay rate for each six (6) minutes that they are late. Members who are less than six minutes late, will not be docked any wages, but will still be counted as reporting late for duty. For example: Up to 5 min., 59 sec. late: 6 min. through 11 min., 59 sec. late: 12 min. through 17 min., 59 sec. late: no loss of pay loss of 1/10 of an hour pay loss of 2/10 of an hour pay, etc.

710.22 The following general policy regarding penalties for lates has been established, and shall be strictly, fairly, and consistently applied to all ranks of the Division of Fire members: One late per 12 month period - Verbal counseling by immediate supervisor, and Form PI-17, Memorandum of Counseling, will be completed. For this purpose, the year will start on the date of the first late. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures Second late in the same 12 month period – The immediate supervisor will complete form PI-13, Personnel Warning Report, and forward it through channels. If the Administrative Officer approves discipline, the member’s immediate supervisor will issue a verbal warning. (Revised 12/31/15) Third late in the same 12 month period – The immediate supervisor will complete form PI-13, Personnel Warning Report, and forward it through channels. If the Administrative Officer approves discipline, the member’s Bureau Head will issue a written reprimand. (Revised 12/31/15) Fourth and any subsequent lates in the same 12 month period - mandatory disciplinary hearing before the Chief of the Division. SICK AND INJURY LEAVE PROCEDURES
712.00 The sick and injury leave policy and procedures of the Division of Fire shall conform to the provisions of this section, in keeping with the dictates of the current Master Salary Ordinance.

712.02 Division members shall be entitled to receive pay while off duty due to sickness or injury unless it is established that such sickness or injury was incurred in the performance of employment other than with the City.

712.04 Members absent from duty, whether due to sickness, injury, or for any other reasons, who neglect to properly report the cause for such absence, may be required to forfeit pay for that period of time during which the absence had not been officially reported and investigated. OFF-DUTY ILLNESS OR INJURY

712.06 Members who become ill or injured or otherwise incapacitated while off duty, and are unable to report for their normal tour of duty, shall contact the Division Fire Alarm Office or utilize TeleStaff to “certify off duty” at least 45 minutes prior to the time that they are required to report for duty. Members failing to notify the Fire Alarm Office or Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures utilize TeleStaff to “certify off duty”, shall be carried on the OF-237 as AWOL. (Revised 12/31/15)

712.08 Members failing to certify off duty at least 45 minutes before roll call may be charged with a “late”, as will be determined by the Administrative Officer, depending upon the circumstances surrounding the incident. (Revised 12/31/15) .

712.09 The procedure for Certifying Off-Duty will be as follows: 1) Via the FAO a. Call (614) 221-2345 b. Notify Operator that you need to COD c. Give Name, ID number and assignment i. If someone else is calling for you, they must give their name and relationship. d. Identify reason for COD from list below: i. ILL ii. INJURED iii. FMLA iv. DIF (Death in Family) (1) Must give relationship v. SLOTS (Sick Leave Other Than Self) vi. LWOP (Leave-Without-Pay Request) e. If not calling from home, give a contact number to the Operator f. If Division help or assistance is needed, ask the Operator to notify the appropriate personnel or office. 2. VIA TeleStaff a. Login to TeleStaff via Mobile App, Telephone, or Computer b. Select the Day needed to COD from Calendar c. Select one of the options (Revised 12/31/15) Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures

712.10 Whenever it is necessary that a member be hospitalized, such member shall be responsible for notifying the Fire Alarm Office and providing information concerning the situation. If the involved member is unable to relay this information, someone in the immediate family should assume this responsibility. The information relayed should include the following: 1. The name of the hospital and room number 2. Reason for member being hospitalized 3. Visitor Status 4. Information concerning time or date or release from hospital (when available) 5. Any other pertinent information that may be useful to the Fire Alarm Office

712.12 Upon receipt of information that a Division member is certified off duty, the Fire Alarm Office shall relay this information to the station or bureau of which the member is assigned. This shall be done as far in advance of the time that such member is normally required to report for duty as is practical. (Revised 12/31/15)

712.14 Information received at a member’s assigned station or bureau pertaining to such member being certified off duty will be entered in the Company Journal and otherwise officially recorded as conditions may warrant. The involved member’s immediate supervisor, or if necessary, other personnel assigned to the station or bureau, shall see that the Battalion Chief -- or other appropriate supervisory Division member -- is notified of the member’s absence as soon as practical, and information regarding the members involved shall be reported to the Payroll and Personnel Office.

712.15 When a member CODs with a LWOP request, they must submit an RT-154 to the Fire Chief as soon as possible, preferably within 48 hours of the incident, identifying the specifics requiring the COD. LWOP is not automatically approved. The member will be on unpaid leave for the hours requested pending approval of the Fire Chief. The member must request LWOP (or the use of some other earned time, i.e. Vacation, Sick Leave, etc.) from the Fire Chief. The Fire Chief may grant this request or decide to charge AWOL and discipline accordingly. (Added 05/01/16) Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures

712.16 When the Battalion Chief or office supervisor is informed that a member assigned to this battalion or office has been certified off duty, he/she shall use his/her judgment in determining the validity of the illness or injury and in deciding the need for verifying the circumstances surrounding the member’s absence. ON-DUTY ILLNESS OR INJURY

712.18 Members who become ill or are injured while on duty shall be taken or sent to an appropriate hospital, their personal healthcare provider, or their home - depending upon the seriousness of the member’s condition.

712.20 When a member becomes ill or is injured while on duty, the immediate supervisor of such member shall be notified as soon as possible. This notification shall be made by the injured member or by other Division members who may have knowledge of the situation.

712.22 The immediate supervisor of the ill or injured member is responsible for notifying the Fire Alarm Office, as well as his/her own immediate superior, and shall also make the necessary entries in the Company Journal or the official bureau or office journal.

712.24 In addition to the preceding requirements, the member’s immediate supervisor shall be required to notify the Emergency Services Deputy Chief, through channels, as soon as possible after the illness or injury occurs.

712.26 When a member is relieved from duty because of illness or injury, the fact shall be reported to the Payroll and Personnel Office. Information relayed shall include the name of the involved member, time and date relieved from duty, and nature of illness or injury.

712.28 It is the responsibility of the Battalion Chief or office supervisor to personally initiate an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the illness or injury, to check on the member’s condition, and to then inform the appropriate bureau head. When necessary, the bureau head shall notify the member’s family. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures

712.30 The immediate supervisor of the ill or injured member shall be responsible for the proper disposition of the member’s car, firefighting gear, personal property, etc., in the event that a member is unable to return to duty.

712.32 On duty members who are to be certified off duty shall report this fact to their immediate supervisor - or shall see that such person is notified - and the supervisor, in turn, shall enter this information into TeleStaff. (Revised 12/31/15) Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures REQUESTING INJURY LEAVE PROCEDURE

712.34 All requests for injury leave shall be submitted to the Administrative Officer AND and Local 67 within seven (7) days of the injury. Requests for injury leave must include the following two (2) items; (Revised 12/31/15) 1. A completed Division of Fire Form PR-5 2. A completed Medical Information Sheet or a doctor's statement which must include: date patient was first seen, description of current disability, dates of any prior treatment for same condition, and actual or expected length of current disability. In addition, the applicable Workman's Compensation forms as provided in the Injury Leave Claims packet will be properly completed and forwarded as per instructions.
712.36 If a request for injury leave is submitted which does not include all of the required items as listed above, the request will not be considered.

712.38 After a determination has been made as to the approval or denial of injury leave, a copy of such decision will be forwarded to the involved employee. If the injury leave is denied, the employee may appeal the decision in writing within 10 days of receipt of the employee's copy of the decision. This appeal shall be submitted through proper channels to the Director of Finance. GENERAL PROVISIONS - SICK AND INJURY LEAVE PROCEDURES

712.42 In the event a member becomes incapacitated and, as a result, is unable to perform the duties required of his position, such member's immediate supervisor shall complete and submit a report of the conditions and circumstances involved. This report shall be forwarded through channels to the Bureau head. After the degree and extent of any disability has been determined by the member's personal physician, the involved member may be placed in a position compatible with the limits of his physical condition. (See "Light Duty Procedures" Section)
712.44 (Deleted 12/31/15) Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures

712.46 In the event that any member of the Division reports a sickness or disability that is feigned or pretended; or if any member shall fraudulently - by concealment, false statement, or otherwise - seek to deceive or mislead Division officials with respect to the particulars or circumstances involved; or if member does not remain at home so as to be visited at the option of a superior officer of the Division, except as provided elsewhere in the Division Rules and Regulations; or if a member refuses or neglects to conform to the instructions governing the actions of all Division members; such member shall be subject to suspension at the discretion of the Chief.

712.48 In all cases where sickness or injury causes a member to be absent from all or any portion of a regularly scheduled tour of duty, Form PR-5 must be completed and submitted through proper channels not later than the second duty day after a member's illness or injury - for those members working the three platoon system - and no later than the third duty day for those members assigned to the 40-hour work week.

712.50 If a member has not returned to duty in time to comply with the provisions of the preceding paragraph, the immediate supervisor of such member shall complete and forward Form PR-5, noting the date and time that "certification off duty" began, the nature of the illness or injury, whether the member is at home or in the hospital, and the anticipated number of days that the member will be absent. If the projected number of days absent is indefinite, this fact shall be stated when filling out Form PR-5.

712.52 Beginning with the seventh (7th) time and each time thereafter, a member is granted sick leave with pay in any calendar year, the first two (2) days of each such leave shall be without pay except as follows: 1. Such absence may, with the approval of the appointing authority, be changed to compensatory time credit or to vacation time. 2. Intermittent periods of sick leave for the same illness or injury, certified by the Director of Public Safety as necessary, shall be counted as one absence if they occur during a period not to exceed thirty (30) calendar days from the date the employee returns to work from the original illness or injury. 3. Death in the immediate family. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures The completed "Medical Appraisal/Return to Duty" letter from the physician will determine if a letter will be sent to the member ordering him/her to report for full duty

712.54 In order for an occurrence of intermittent illness or injury to be counted as one incident as described in 712.52.b, the following procedures shall be followed: 1. Division of Fire Form PR-5 must be completed and submitted through proper channels. The member must identify the previous date on which sick leave with pay was granted and must request that the present illness be counted as one incident. 2. The member must attach a doctor's statement to the Form PR-5 which states the later illness or injury is a result of the same circumstances that caused the earlier illness or injury for which sick leave with pay was granted. SICK LEAVE CERTIFICATION

712.55 The Personnel Office will issue a Certified Letter to any member who is on sick leave after six (6) consecutive duty days, and/or after the sixth and each succeeding sick leave incident in a payroll calendar year. The letter will request that the member provide a doctor's excuse explaining the reason for the member's absence and a projected return to work date. The member will have ten (10) calendar days to submit this information to the Personnel Office. If a response from the member has not been received within ten (10) calendar days, he/she may be charged “Absent without Leave” (AWOL). (Revised 12/31/15) If the member's response is that he/she will be on sick/injury leave for an extended period, a "Medical Appraisal/Return to Duty" letter, to be completed by the physician, will be sent to the member. This letter requests the physician to evaluate the member's ability to return to duty or light duty, if applicable. If the "Medical Appraisal/Return to Duty" letter is not received in the Personnel Office within fifteen (15) calendar days of its receipt by the member, the Division will solicit assistance from the City's Risk Management Office to obtain medical information, and may schedule the member for an independent medical examination with a City physician. Failure to provide medical documentation and/or recertification may result in the denial of sick leave. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures or light duty. If the member requests a light duty assignment, a physician's excuse with an approximate return to full duty date must be submitted. (Revised 12/31/15)

712.55.1 Human Resources will send an FMLA packet to any member who is on sick leave after three (3) consecutive duty days. The member will have fifteen (15) calendar days to contact Human Resources and submit the completed FMLA form or other medical documentation. If a response from the member has not been received within fifteen (15) calendar days, his or her sick leave may be disapproved and the Fire Chief may require evidence as to the adequacy of the reason for the employees absence during the time for which sick leave is requested. (Revised 12/31/15)

712.55.2 Any member who is on sick leave after six (6) consecutive duty days, will be contacted by Human Resources and required to provide a doctor’s excuse explaining the reason for the member’s absence and a projected return to work date. (Revised 12/31/15)

712.55.3 If the member’s response is that he/she will be on sick/injury leave for an extended period, a “Medical Appraisal/Return to Duty” letter, to be completed by the physician, will be sent to the member. This letter requests the physician to evaluate the member’s ability to return to duty or light duty, if applicable. If the “Medical Appraisal/Return to Duty” letter is not received by Human Resources within fifteen (15) calendar days of its receipt by the member, the Division will solicit assistance from the City’s Risk Management Office to obtain medical information, and may schedule the member for an independent medical examination with a City physician. Failure to provide medical documentation and/or recertification may result in the denial of sick leave. (Revised 12/31/15)

712.55.4 The completed “Medical Appraisal/Return to Duty” letter from the physician will determine if a letter will be sent to the member ordering him/her to report for full duty or light duty. (Revised 12/31/15) Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures LIGHT DUTY PROCEDURES

712.56 Light duty assignments are specifically created temporary job assignments for members injured or otherwise incapacitated. Such light duty assignments are temporary assignments only, are not vacant or permanent positions within the Division’s workforce, and are not available to employees on a permanent basis under any circumstances. (Revised 12/31/15) 1. Light duty is not automatically granted to Division members. Assignments are based on the needs of the Division of Fire. The Administrative Bureau Chief is responsible for authorizing light duty assignments. Members will be notified if or when their request has been approved. (Revised 12/31/15) 2. To request to have a light duty assignment made within a Bureau, the Bureau Head must notify the Administrative Office of the need to have work completed and provide a description of that work. (Revised 12/31/15) 3. Job assignments for light duty members will be determined by the skills of the member and/or the needs of the Division. If the member’s restrictions cannot be accommodated by the Division, the member must use their available existing leave balances or they may be carried on injury leave, if applicable. (Revised 12/31/15) 4. Members who are incapable of performing their regular duties due to a work related injury or illness, but capable of performing duties in a limited capacity, shall request a light duty assignment. (Revised 12/31/15) 5. It is the policy of the Division of Fire that pregnant members may continue to participate in the work force during pregnancy. For purposes of this policy, a pregnancy related disability is treated as a non-work related injury or illness. Pregnant members who are able to work are that a corrective performance counseling session is necessary. Therefore, supervisors permitted to do so under the same conditions as other employees if they are able to fully perform their regularly assigned job duties. The pregnant member is responsible, with the advice of their physician, to determine how long they will continue working in their assigned position. A pregnant member is not required to Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures request or accept a light duty assignment. However, they are encouraged to consider a light duty assignment because of the unpredictable nature of emergency responses. The pregnant member may request light duty at any time during their pregnancy by following the light duty procedures. (Revised 12/31/15)

712.58 To work a light duty assignment, a member must adhere to the following requirements: 1. Light duty requests should be submitted directly to the Administrative Office no less than one week before the anticipated start date and must include the following: (Revised 12/31/15) a. A completed RT-154, Intra-Divisional Communication, requesting a light duty assignment. The RT-154 needs to be typed, include the start date being requested, the reason for requesting and whether or not the light duty is for a work related injury. (For members who have a platoon assignment, the start date will always be on the Sunday of the Kelly Day cycle they will start). (Revised 12/31/15) b. A completed doctor’s statement, Medco-14 or similar form, which must include the date the member is eligible to work with restrictions, the details of all restrictions placed upon the member, whether the restrictions are temporary or permanent, as well as the date when the member is expected to return to regular duty. (Should a member not want to submit their medical documentation to the Administrative Office, they may instead submit it directly to the Division of Fire Human Resource Office) (Revised 12/31/15) 2. Members must have a doctor’s statement on file with the Administrative Office or the Division of Fire Human Resource Office for the duration of their light duty assignment. Failure to provide an appropriate doctor’s statement will result in denial of the member’s light duty assignment. The Division reserves the right to request additional medical documentation at any time during a member’s light duty assignment. (Revised 12/31/15) Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures 3. Light duty assignments for members permanently assigned to a platoon assignment will begin and end on the Sunday of the Kelly Day cycle. This requirement will not apply to members permanently assigned to a 40 hour assignment. (Revised 12/31/15) 4. Members on light duty will generally be assigned to a 40 hour workweek. The work schedule will consist of an eight hour day, Monday thru Friday. The work hours will be between 0700 and 1600, as determined by the Bureau Head. (Revised 12/31/15) 5. The 40 hour, 8% stipend, will not be paid to members on a light duty assignment. Exceptions will be to those individuals who were being paid the 8% stipend prior to approval for Light Duty. Members on light duty are not eligible for shift differential, OOC, Special Duty or Special Events. (Revised 12/31/15) 6. Additionally, members on light duty may not accept a turn of overtime. The member’s vacation hours will be converted to a 40 hour equivalent balance and vacation will be accrued and charged at the 40 hour rate. (Revised 12/31/15) 7. Members on light duty may be offered position specific training to accommodate Division’s needs. (Revised 12/31/15) 8. Vacation may be taken in one hour increments. Prior approval is required. (Revised 12/31/15) 9. Sick or injury leave may be taken in one hour increments. When a member is absent for all or any portion of a regularly scheduled tour of duty due to a sickness or an injury leave related matter the member must submit a PR-5. This includes but is not limited to: doctor visits, physical therapy, and Industrial Commission hearings that occur during normal duty hours. (Revised 12/31/15) Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures 10. Light duty members that need to COD (certify off duty) are to follow the normal call off procedures as detailed in the Systems Manual. (Revised 12/31/15) 11. Members on light-duty shall not use division fitness equipment without a medical release and signed authorization from the Administrative Bureau Chief or designee. When so authorized, the following procedure shall apply: a. Submit a completed medical release form from your attending physician. The medical release form is provided by the Division and must indicate the type of exercise and/or physical equipment as recommended for physical therapy. Details should include weight restrictions and exercise duration as applicable. (Revised 12/31/15) b. Submit a typed RT-154, Intra-Divisional Communication, to the Administrative Bureau Chief requesting to participate in a physical fitness program. Attach the medical release form from the attending physician to the RT-154. (Revised 12/31/15) c. When using the division’s fitness center members on a light duty assignment are required to document their time by signing in and out. (Revised 12/31/15) 12. The Bureau where the member works a light duty assignment will record his/her daily activity on their OF-237, in the “Other” column, with a note in the remarks section. When the member returns to regular duty, the Bureau that provided the light duty assignment will report this fact in the remarks section of the OF-237. The place of permanent assignment shall continue to report the member on light duty, on their OF-237, each duty day until the members return to regular duty. (Revised 12/31/15) Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures Division personnel working the forty-hour week who are absent from work due to illness for more than two (2) consecutive working days must present a written

712.60 To return to regular duty, a member must adhere to the following: 1. Requests to return to regular duty need to be made in advance to the Administrative Office and must include the following: a. A completed RT-154, Intra-Divisional Communication, requesting to be released from the light duty assignment. The RT-154 needs to be typed and include the date that the member will be returning to regular duty. (For members who have a platoon assignment, the return to work date needs to be on or before the Sunday of the Kelly Day cycle they will be released) (Revised 12/31/15) b. A completed doctor’s statement, Medco-14 or similar form, which must include the date the member is released to return to regular duty and state that the member is capable of returning to regular duty. (Revised 12/31/15) 2. The Administrative Office will notify the appropriate Bureau Head when the request to return to regular duty is approved. (Added 12/31/15)

712.62 The Fire Chief or designee shall review the status of members who are unable to consistently perform their regularly assigned duties for a 1 year period. The Fire Chief may cause an investigation to determine fitness for duty. To determine fitness for duty Division members shall be required to participate in an interactive process and produce medical documentation from the member’s physician or appropriate attending medical professional and/or undergo examination by an appropriate medical professional designated by the city. (Added 12/31/15) RETURNING TO REGULAR DUTY FROM ILLNESS OR INJURY PROCEDURE

714.t: Returning To Duty From Illness Or Injury
p: 714.00 Division members returning to their regular duty assignments after having been off duty for reasons of injury or illness shall comply with the provisions of this section, and with the applicable portions of the current Master Salary Ordinance. 714.02 Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures statement from their personal physician, to their immediate supervisor, affirming that they are able to return to duty. Members who have been absent due to illness for two (2) days or less may return to duty without a statement from their physician.

714.04 Division personnel working the platoon system who have been absent due to illness for more than one (1) tour of duty must present a written statement from their personal physician, to their immediate supervisor, in order to return to duty. A member absent due to illness for one (1) complete tour of duty or less, may be allowed to return to duty if, in the opinion of such member's immediate supervisor or bureau head, the member in question is able to properly discharge his assigned duties.

714.06 Division members who have been absent from their regularly assigned duties because of an on-duty injury - including those members who have been temporarily assigned to "light duty" positions - must obtain the written approval of a physician and present this statement to their immediate supervisor upon returning to regular duty.

714.08 If in the opinion of their immediate supervisor, members desiring to return to regular duty are not able to perform the duties required of his or her job assignment, such supervisor shall immediately notify the Administrative Officer (through channels) of this fact. The Administrative Officer will then schedule an appointment at an appropriate facility for the purpose of examining the involved member. Grant Hospital personnel will make the final determination as to whether the member may return to regular duty. If necessary, the on-duty Deputy Chief will make any immediate interim decisions regarding the status of such employees. (Revised 12/31/15)
714.10 All physicians’ statements or other related documents shall be attached to a completed PR-5 and submitted through channels. SICK LEAVE OTHER THAN SELF PROCEDURE

714.12 Sick Leave Other Than Self (SL/OTS) is defined as leave utilized because of the illness or medically related dependency of a member of the employee's immediate family, living in the employee's household. "Immediate Family" is defined in the current Master Salary Ordinance. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures

714.14 Uniformed members returning to work after having been off duty for reasons of utilizing "Sick Leave Other Than Self" (regardless of the time period involved) shall be required to submit a certified statement from the attending physician, to the Chief, stating that their presence was required at home.

714.16 Non-uniformed members returning to work after having been off duty for reasons of utilizing "Sick Leave Other Than Self" may be required to submit a certificate from a licensed physician, or a satisfactory written statement signed by the involved member, to the Chief, stating the nature of the illness. 716.02 Physical examinations may be requested by individual Bureau Heads, when a special need is indicated, subject to the approval of the Chief. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures EMPLOYEE COUNSELING PROCEDURES

720.00 Counseling is one of the key elements of leadership. It is the art of communicating advice, instruction, or judgment, with the intent of influencing a person's attitude or behavior. Counseling is a responsibility of immediate supervisors and should be conducted periodically. GOOD PERFORMANCE COUNSELING

720.02 One important aspect of counseling is that it should not be used solely to point out and attempt to improve job performance or conduct. If employees are to maintain a high level of motivation and performance it is important to satisfy the need for self-esteem. Through counseling for good performance the immediate supervisor can at least partially satisfy this need.

720.04 In counseling for good performance, try to be specific in order to emphasize and reinforce that which is particularly noteworthy. In this way the employee will be rewarded for good performance and will, because of the personal satisfaction gained, want to repeat this performance.

720.06 Good performance counseling may range from a "pat on the back" for doing a good job to the more formal actions of (1) writing a letter of commendation to be placed in the employee's official file, or (2) recommending the employee for an award pursuant to Chapter III, Sections 330.00-330.82 of this manual. NO special documentation is required or necessary for good performance counseling. CORRECTIVE PERFORMANCE COUNSELING

720.08 At times, an immediate supervisor may be faced with an employee whose job performance or conduct is below standard. If this occurs the supervisor must not allow these problems to slide. Inaction is not the answer because it may turn small difficulties into major disruptions. When the immediate supervisor first becomes aware that a job performance or conduct problem exists, the supervisor should conduct corrective counseling. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures

720.10 The goal of corrective performance counseling is to improve the job performance or conduct of the employee. It is a process for assisting the employee in taking the steps necessary to correct job performance or correct deficiencies.

720.12 Corrective performance counseling can range from the informal discussion to the formal session which is documented with a Memorandum of Counseling. Whichever type counseling is used it is important that the session be conducted in private, both to prevent distractions and to maintain a confidential atmosphere.

720.14 It would be impossible to list all of the reasons which might indicate to the supervisor that a corrective performance counseling session is necessary. Therefore, supervisors must know their employees well enough to recognize when they need to be counseled. Some indications that supervisors must learn to recognize are: 1. When a probationary employee or apprentice firefighter is having difficulty learning or performing necessary elements of the job. 2. When a previously good performer begins to perform below par consistently. 3. When a normally attentive employee suddenly displays a lack of attentiveness or concentration which adversely affects job performance. 4. When an employee is involved in deliberate acts of misconduct or refuses to follow orders or instructions. 5. When an employee abuses or exhibits a disregard for the rules, regulations, policies or procedures of the Division of Fire, or the City of Columbus, or the Civil Service Commission.

720.16 The decision of whether to conduct informal or formal corrective performance counseling is left to the discretion of the immediate supervisor. Normally a formal counseling session will be held only after one or more informal sessions covering the specific problem have failed to correct or improve performance or conduct. However, if the job performance or conduct is substantially below acceptable standards, or in the case of a probationary employee or apprentice firefighter, the supervisor may elect to use the formal counseling session when the problem is first discovered. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures CONDUCTING THE FORMAL COUNSELING SESSION

720.18 During the formal counseling session, the supervisor should structure the discussion using the Memorandum of Counseling as a guide. Without being too forceful the supervisor can invite the employee back from detours, escapes, fruitless conversation, etc., by the use of brief questions. It is important to remember that the goal of the counseling session is to correct shortcomings in job performance or conduct, not to cause embarrassment. Under no circumstances should the supervisor allow himself to be trapped into an argument with the person being counseled.

720.20 After each paragraph of the Memorandum of Counseling has been thoroughly explained and discussed, and it is apparent that the purpose of the counseling session has been accomplished, steps should be taken to close the conversation in a friendly manner. The session should be closed when all points have been covered and when the employee has had ample time and opportunity to understand the steps he or she must take in order to correct the job performance or conduct deficiency.

720.22 After the counseling session is over the supervisor must continue to evaluate job performance or conduct. The supervisor must check to ensure that satisfactory progress is being made to correct the shortcomings discussed during the counseling session. If satisfactory progress is not being made, further formal counseling or other steps may become necessary. EMPLOYEE ASSISTANCE PROGRAM

720.24 During the counseling discussion the employee may tell the supervisor of a personal situation which is affecting job performance or conduct. Or, short of an admission, the conversation may lead the supervisor to suspect this as the reason for a performance or conduct deficiency. If this situation occurs, the supervisor should refer the employee to the City's Employee Assistance Program.

720.26 If the employee refuses to participate in the Employee Assistance Program, or agrees to participate and then does not keep appointments, or the rehabilitative efforts do not result in improved performance or conduct to an acceptable level, then the supervisor must consider initiating other appropriate personnel action. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures DOCUMENTATION

720.28 Documentation of corrective performance counseling is the key to developing an adequate record of what occurred at the immediate supervisory level. This will be accomplished through the use of the Memorandum of Counseling.

720.30 Whenever corrective performance counseling fails to correct or improve job performance or conduct the situation may eventually require initiation of formal disciplinary action. If this occurs the employee may raise the defense that he or she was never informed of a job performance or conduct problem, and/or was never informed of the steps to take in order to correct the problem. Proper documentation can be used to counter that defense. There is no excuse for waiting until disciplinary action is formally proposed to try to develop documentation that should have been developed at an earlier stage.

720.32 The Memorandum of Counseling is one source of documentation of the efforts the immediate supervisor made to assist the employee. It is the first step in establishing that the job performance or conduct deficiencies were communicated to the employee, that the steps necessary to correct the deficiencies were communicated to the employee, and that the employee was afforded a reasonable time to demonstrate acceptable performance or conduct.

720.34 It will not be required or necessary for the immediate supervisor to document good performance counseling or informal corrective performance counseling. To require this would create an unreasonable administrative burden and generate unnecessary paperwork.

720.36 For a formal corrective performance counseling session the immediate supervisor will be required to properly complete and distribute the Memorandum of Counseling. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures MEMORANDUM OF COUNSELING

720.38 Only one specific performance or conduct problem will be listed on a memorandum. Normally the corrective performance counseling session will cover only one or two such problems. Most problems of this nature can be corrected through the use of informal counseling sessions. Furthermore, the supervisor should not allow several serious deficiencies to accumulate and then issue several memoranda at one counseling session.

720.40 The supervisor should complete the heading and paragraphs 1 and 2 of the Memorandum of Counseling prior to holding the counseling session. If additional space is needed, one or more sheets of paper can be attached to this memorandum. The supervisor must initial and date each attached sheet.

720.42 After thoroughly discussing paragraphs 1, 2, and 3 with the employee, the supervisor must decide whether or not to refer the employee to the City Employee Assistance Program. This election is indicated by the supervisor in paragraph 4. The supervisor will sign and date the memorandum.

720.46 The supervisor should then (1) explain the acknowledgment paragraph to the employee, (2) explain that the employee has a right to have a copy of the memorandum forwarded to the Union and that this right can be exercised only if the employee checks the appropriate box on the memorandum, and (3) request the employee to sign and date the memorandum. If the employee refuses to sign the supervisor will check the appropriate box and sign and date in the space provided.

720.48 The supervisor shall be responsible for providing the employee with a copy of the completed memorandum. If the employee elects to have the Union receive a copy, the supervisor shall provide the appropriate Union Steward with a copy. The supervisor shall keep the original until the performance or conduct problem is satisfactory resolved. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures FUNERAL PROCEDURES

726.00 When death occurs to an on-duty firefighter, the on-duty Deputy Chief (ES 2) is responsible for ensuring that personal notification is made to the deceased's family. This personal notification may be made by the on-duty Deputy Chief (ES 2), a designated Battalion Chief or a close family friend and, if possible, with the aid of one or both Division of Fire Chaplains.
726.02 The procedure set forth in 726.00 will be followed if the Division of Fire is informed of the death of an off-duty firefighter before the family is aware of the situation.
726.04 In either of the above situations, the Fire Chief and the Administrative Officer will be notified immediately. (Revised 12/31/15)

726.06 The on-duty Deputy Chief (ES-2) IS responsible for obtaining the information necessary to complete the "Funeral Notice" Form PI-15 and ensuring that this information is transmitted to the Fire Alarm Office for Public Address Transmission to all stations. This procedure will also be followed when the Division of Fire is informed of the death of a retired firefighter. (Revised 12/31/15)

726.08 The Deputy Chief (ES-2) will see that an offer of transportation is made to the family of a firefighter who was on current paid status to assist in making any necessary funeral arrangements and to transport the next-of-kin to the Bureau of Administration to take care of insurance, severance pay, pension, etc.
726.10 The Deputy Chief (ES-2) on-duty the first viewing day will order flowers to be sent to the funeral home from the Division of Fire.

726.12 The Deputy Chief (ES 2) on-duty each viewing day will arrange for an Honor Guard at the funeral home if the member was on current paid status and the family so requests. (Revised 12/31/15) Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures
726.12.1 The Emergency Services Deputy Chiefs (ES 2) should maintain a roster of Honor Guard members in accordance with Section 334.08 of the Systems Manual. (Revised 12/31/15)

726.16 Military Honors and uniform turnouts are not offered for retired personnel as a general rule, but under special circumstances may be authorized by the Fire Chief. (Revised 12/31/15) MILITARY LEAVE PROCEDURES
728.00 The military leave policy and procedures of the Division of Fire shall conform to the provisions of the current Labor Agreement between the City of Columbus and Local #67 IAFF.

728.06 Any member of the Division of Fire who is applying for military leave shall complete Form PR-2 and forward it through proper channels to the Chief accompanied with a copy of their military orders.
728.08 Application should be submitted at least three (3) working days prior to the effective date of military leave. (Revised 12/31/15)

728.10 A military pay voucher shall be submitted to the Division of Fire Payroll Office no later than the first regularly scheduled workday after returning from military leave. This voucher must show the total days of military leave and the total base pay received. The amount of the base pay will be deducted from the next regular Division of Fire check on the pay following the members return to duty. 734.00 Special Leave procedures of the Division of Fire shall conform to the provisions of this section and the current Labor Agreement between the City of Columbus and Local #67, IAFF.
734.02 All requests for Special Leave shall be submitted on Form PR-9 at least 2 working days in advance.
734.04 Jury Duty Leave: Division employees shall be permitted time off while serving upon a jury in any court of record in Franklin County or adjoining counties.

734.05 Any employee serving jury duty shall obtain a City of Columbus, Jury Duty Report Form from the Division Administrative Officer before the starting date of jury duty. The form shall be completed daily during the course of jury duty and submitted to the Administrative Officer immediately upon completion of jury duty. (Revised 12/31/15)
734.06 Uniformed members will be paid their regular salary less whatever amount such member may receive as compensation for his services. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures

734.08 Non-uniformed members will be paid their regular salary for the period of time served as a juror. They will also be paid by the court for their services. All payments received for duty service during regular working hours shall be submitted to the Bureau of Administration as soon as possible.

734.10 Examination Leave: Division employees shall be permitted time off with pay for participation in Civil Service tests for taking required examinations pertinent to their employment with the City of Columbus.
734.12 Court Leave: Division employees shall be permitted time off with pay when required to attend court as a witness for the City of Columbus.

734.14 Employees appearing in court, EXCEPT FRANKLIN COUNTY MUNICIPAL COURT, as a witness for the City, will receive payment from the court for their service. This payment will be made in the form of a certificate of fees, which shall not be cashed, but endorsed and forwarded through channels to the Bureau of Administration as soon as possible. Any travel or other daily costs awarded by the court shall also be submitted to the Bureau of Administration.
734.16 Any questions concerning the collection of any witness fees, or fees issued for other services rendered, shall be directed to the Administrative Office. (Revised 12/31/15)

734.18 Miscellaneous Leave: Time off with pay may also be granted for reasons such as attending classes at approved educational institutions, certain Union business, benevolent duties or other such activities approved by the Chief. (Revised 12/31/15)

734.20 Time off involving non-fire Division activities such as those mentioned above, will not be granted if such time off would result in an engine or ladder company running with less than four (4) people after 2000 hours.

736.00 Any record held by the Division of Fire is a public record.

736.02 “Public record” means a record kept by a public office. “Record” means: (1) any document, device, or item, regardless of physical form or characteristic, including an electronic record; (2) created or received by, or coming under the jurisdiction of any public office of a political subdivision; (3) which serves to document the organization, functions, policies, decisions, procedures, operations, or other activities of the office. (Revised 12/31/15)
736.04 Prior to releasing Division records, Division members shall review the provisions for accessing or releasing public records as provided in this section.

736.06 The Fire Division Forms List, published in section 738.00, identifies the Official Division Record Keeper and a Secondary Record Keeper. Only the Official Division Record Keeper, identified in the Fire Division Forms List, or his/her designee, may provide copies of, or access to, a Division record.

736.08 The Secondary Record Keeper is any Division member who maintains a copy of Division record. Although the Fire Division Forms List identifies only one Secondary Record Keeper, others may exist. The Secondary Record Keeper will direct persons requesting a copy of a report or form to the Official Division Record Keeper.
736.10 The Secondary Record Keeper shall provide replacement copies, if available, to the Official Division Record Keeper upon request. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures
736.12 The applicable Official Division Record Keeper, or designee, shall consult section 736.28 for the proper access method prior to providing access to files, forms or records. RETENTION

736.14 Division records and forms are legally defined as Public Records. As such, certain records and forms are permanent documents that must be retained indefinitely. Others may be disposed of, after they have served their intended purpose.

736.16 The Fire Division Forms List, published in section 738.00, identifies all the Division’s forms and the retention period for each. Before disposing of any Division records, the Fire Division Forms List will be consulted to determine the applicable retention period.

736.18 Disposal of records shall be done in accordance with existing procedures established by the Fire Division and the City of Columbus. ADMINISTRATIVE ACCESS
736.20 The public records access procedure is not meant to restrict access by Division personnel in the course of legitimate Division business.
736.24 Division members, acting on behalf of the individuals listed above, must present written authorization from that individual on an RT-154 to obtain the specific record requested.
736.26 Division members, using their official position to obtain records for reasons outside their official capacity, will be subject to discipline. ACCESS TO DIVISION RECORDS

736.28 Division members and members of the public requesting access to or copies of, Division records will be asked to complete the appropriate Division form: 1. Request for Public Record/Report (form RR-164) (Added 12/31/15) 2. Photo Request (form RI-163)

736.30 Access to public records may be restricted due to nature of the information. The Division has specific access methods for the following record types: “A” Typical Public Records “B” Medical Records “C” Confidential Law Enforcement Investigatory Records

736.32 Access methods, for all Division forms are listed in the Fire Division Forms List published in section 738.00. Some Division records have multiple sections, and each section may fall under a different access method. 736.34 Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures RECORD KEEPER

736.36 An Official Division Record Keeper has been designated for each Bureau and some specific offices. The Official Division Record Keeper is responsible for all aspects of records retention and disposition within that Bureau or Office. All record requests should go through an Official Division Record Keeper or designee. Any Secondary Record Keeper shall direct requests for access to records to the Official Division Record Keeper. BUREAU OR OFFICE Office of the Chief Administration Emergency Services Support Services Fire Prevention Personnel Training OFFICIAL DIVISION RECORD KEEPER Administrative Officer Administrative Analyst Bureau Head Maintenance Officer Records Officer (Prevention 10) Personnel Manager Bureau Head
736.38 (Deleted 12/31/15) ACCOUNTABILITY

736.40 The Official Division Record Keeper is responsible for maintaining a record of all Requests for Public Record/Report (RR-164) and Photo Request (RI-163) for five years, or the life of the record, whichever is greater. If, due to the nature of the record, a copy of the RR-164 or RI-163 cannot be kept with the record, an office ledger or folder containing the request forms shall be maintained by the Official Division Record Keeper.
736.42 Any records known to be associated with an ongoing investigation may not be viewed or copied without the express permission of the Fire Chief.
736.44 - 736.52 (Deleted 12/31/15) Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures ACCESS METHOD “C” -- CONFIDENTIAL LAW ENFORCEMENT / INVESTIGATORY RECORDS

736.54 The Ohio Revised Code Section 149.43 Paragraph 2, Sections a, b, c, and d states: Records that pertain to a law enforcement matter of a criminal, quasi-criminal, civil, or administrative nature and that, if released, would create a high probability of disclosing the identity of an uncharged suspect, the identity of a confidential source, information that would endanger the life or physical safety of law enforcement personnel, a crime victim, a witness, or a confidential information source, specific confidential investigatory techniques or procedures, or specific investigatory work product, are exempt from disclosure as confidential law enforcement investigatory records.

736.56 A request for the records of an ongoing or pending criminal, quasi-criminal, civil, or administrative nature shall be made in written form. The Investigator handling the case will be contacted. That Investigator and his/her chain of command will make the decision, whether the case is exempt from release per O.R.C. 149.43 or other applicable State or Federal Law. If the chain of command determines the information being requested is exempt from public disclosure, the records and the RR-164 and /or RI-163 will be presented to the Fire Chief for a final determination. 742.t: 742.00 An unpaid leave of absence occurs when a member is AWOL, on LWO
p: 742.00 An unpaid leave of absence occurs when a member is AWOL, on LWOP, or serving a Suspension.
742.02 AWOL (absent without leave) 1. Unapproved absence form duty. 2. Unpaid status. 3. Subject to disciplinary action.

742.04 LWOP (leave without pay) 1. Pre-approved absence from duty in accordance with the provisions of Article 29 of the current contract. Any other absence will be considered AWOL. 2. Must be approved by the Chief. 3. Unpaid status.
742.06 Suspension 1. Absent as a result of disciplinary action. 2. Unpaid status.

742.08 Members shall monitor their sick leave and vacation balances to ensure they have sufficient time to cover their absences. Members who have exhausted their vacation and sick leave cannot arbitrarily opt to “go off the payroll” without prior approval of the Chief. Personnel not reporting for duty in this situation will be considered AWOL.

742.12 Members must ask for and receive approval for FMLA leave prior to taking time off, except in emergency situations. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures SUBPOENA/SUMMONS PROCEDURES

750.00 Fire Division personnel are subject to being subpoenaed or summoned to provide testimony in a variety of civil and criminal court actions. This section contains information and guidelines designated to assist Division members who are called upon to participate in these proceedings. (from 560.00 - Revised 12/31/15)

750.02 Any Division member receiving a summons or subpoena is legally responsible for acknowledging and answering such citation. Failure to react to same could result in a penalty. Members should be certain to report to the designated courtroom or other specified location on time, as being late could result in a contempt charge or cause the case to be dismissed. (from 560.02 - Revised 12/31/15)

750.04 Normally, subpoenas and summonses are initially received at Fire Division Headquarters and forwarded through regular Division channels to the involved personnel. Members receiving these documents shall notify their immediate supervisors as soon as possible, relaying the particulars of the subpoena/summons and noting any possible scheduling conflicts that may be involved. (from 560.04 - Revised 12/31/15)

750.06 Each subpoena or summons will list the appearance date and time, the court address and courtroom number, the defendant's name, the plaintiff's name, and the name of the prosecutor or attorney who issued the notification. In addition, the complaint or charges will usually be listed. (from 560.06 - Revised 12/31/15)

750.08 Division members receiving summonses or subpoenas shall be required to promptly determine the circumstances of the incident involved. If the subject matter is not known or cannot be readily recalled, the person issuing the document should be contacted. Members shall ascertain the date and address of the incident, names of all parties involved, nature of the incident, and the subject matter that they may be required to address. (from 560.08 - Revised 12/31/15) Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VII Division Personnel Procedures

750.12 Civil cases might involve such things as fire incidents, medical incidents, accidents involving fire apparatus, or suits of just about any nature. The Division bureau involved should be contacted in order to ascertain the present status of the particular case and the official position of that bureau. In any case where the situation is questionable and/or may possibly be detrimental to either the City, Division of Fire, any fire personnel, the general public, or to the holding of an open criminal investigation, the concerned Bureau Head will discuss the matter with a representative of the City Attorney's Office. Members should not discuss details of any case in which they are involved with anyone other than those Division members and designated legal representatives who are directly involved with the case. (from 560.12 - Revised 12/31/15) COURTROOM APPEARANCE PROCEDURES

750.14 Members called upon to appear in court for any purpose associated with their employment with the Division of Fire shall wear the appropriate dress uniform as indicated by their current duty assignment. Any deviation from this requirement will take place only with the expressed permission of the involved member's bureau head. (from 560.14 - Revised 05/01/16)

750.18 Juvenile Court: Members should report to the front desk, identify themselves, and ask for the number of the courtroom in which the case in question is scheduled to be heard. Then report to the prosecutor or bailiff at that courtroom.
