800.00 It is the policy of the City of Columbus that the public has the right to expect persons employed by the City in its Fire Division will be free from the effects of drugs and alcohol. The City, as the employer, has the right to expect its members to report for work fit and able for duty and to set a positive example for the community. The purposes of this policy shall be achieved in such manner as not to violate any established constitutional rights of the members of the Fire Division.

800.02 The Columbus Fire Division (CFD) has as its primary objective to provide the safest and most efficient public services possible for Central Ohio residents. Among the multitude of factors influencing its ability to accomplish this, no variable has a more significant impact than maintaining members who are physically fit, mentally healthy and alert onthe-job. Naturally, being free from the effects of drugs or alcohol is a requisite for achieving this, and as such, is a condition of employment with CFD. The CFD strives for a drug-free work environment to ensure a safe workplace for all members and to minimize job performance problems throughout its workforce.

800.04 To accomplish these objectives, all members will be subject to drug testing under the circumstances set forth in the Collective Bargaining Agreement between the IAFF and the City of Columbus. A member's refusal to submit to such testing upon request will be considered a positive test. A member who submits an altered test sample will be considered to have tested positive. A member who tested positive for the presence of drugs or alcohol will not be permitted to return to work until after he/she has passed a return-to-duty drug/alcohol test. The collective bargaining agreement has established a disciplinary policy that clearly defines prohibited conduct and the consequences of its violation. The CFD has contained the disciplinary policy in Section 846.00-846.10 of this Manual.

800.06 Specifically, possessing, using, selling, purchasing, manufacturing, dispensing of any illegal drug by CFD members is strictly prohibited. Violations of the above regulations create serious safety risk to the public, co-workers, and the member and therefore are Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VIII Substance Abuse Policy and Procedures grounds for action. In addition, reporting to work or working under the influence of alcohol as defined by the collective bargaining agreement is strictly prohibited.

800.08 Due to many factors, including the lingering effects of alcohol, it is difficult for any individual to be certain of his/her own blood alcohol content (BAC) following alcohol consumption. Therefore, for a member to ensure that, while working, he/she is within the numerical BAC limit established in this policy, CFD requires that members not use alcoholic beverages during breaks, lunch period, or four (4) hours prior to reporting for duty.

800.10 Off-duty use of illegal substances can have a profound impact upon a member's productivity, and other aspects of job performance. These factors have the potential to adversely affect the CFD both on an immediate and long-term basis. For these reasons, it is prohibited for members to have illegal drugs in their systems as detected by urine tests above the positive level as set forth in the collective bargaining agreement.

800.12 A member who is using therapeutic (i.e. prescription) or over-the-counter medications must report the required use of such medications to his/her supervisor prior to the beginning of the member's shift if the substance could impair coordination, cause drowsiness, or could otherwise interfere with the safe performance of duties..

800.14 A third party vendor shall administer all drug and alcohol testing. The City and Local IAFF 67 shall mutually agree upon the vendor. The drug and alcohol testing is designed to treat all members subject to such testing in a fair and impartial manner, according to the terms and conditions set forth in the collective bargaining agreement. APPLICABILITY

802.t: 802.00 All uniformed employees in the bargaining unit whose terms and
p: 802.00 All uniformed employees in the bargaining unit whose terms and conditions of employment are governed by the current Collective Bargaining Agreement shall be subject to drug and alcohol testing. Members are responsible for adhering to this policy without exception. Officers will be held strictly accountable for fair and consistent enforcement of the Drug and Alcohol Testing Policy. The policy shall be applied in an impartial and non- discriminatory manner. Any officer who knowingly fails to enforce Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VIII Substance Abuse Policy and Procedures the requirement of this policy or intentionally misuses the policy in regard to subordinates will be subject to disciplinary action. MEDICAL REVIEW PHYSICIAN (MRP)

804.00 The Medical Review Physician will be a licensed physician who is familiar with the characteristics of the tests used, and will be the sole person responsible for the initial receipt, evaluation, and interpretation of the test results. The City and Local IAFF 67 mutually agree upon the Medical Review Physician. If the test results are initially determined to be positive, the MRP shall examine alternate medical explanations for any positive test results. This may include conduction of a medical interview with the affected employee, review of the employee's medical history, review of any current prescribed medication, review of the chain of custody and review any other relevant biomedical factors. The MRP will review all medical records made available by the tested employee. An employee shall be expected to cooperate promptly with the MRP.

804.02 The MRP may verify a test as positive without interviewing the effected employee if more than 5 days elapse after the MRP first attempts to contact the employee. Once the MRP determines that the test is an actual positive then he/she will contact the Fire Chief or designee to notify of the positive test result.

804.04 The Human Resources Department has hired a Drug and Alcohol Coordinator (DAC) to perform the coordinating of testing duties associated with the citywide drug and alcohol testing. This includes the CFD drug and alcohol program.
804.06 The DAC shall coordinate aspects of the CFD drug and alcohol program, i.e., receiving test results, keeping records, and providing technical assistance to CFD. EDUCATION AND TRAINING

806.00 To increase member awareness of the potential dangers and consequences of substance abuse in the workplace, the members will be provided with education and training. All CFD members will be given training regarding the Substance Abuse Policy. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VIII Substance Abuse Policy and Procedures

806.02 Officers and firefighters who routinely work out of classification as supervisors, who are responsible for making reasonable suspicion testing referrals, will be provided with additional training on a yearly basis. This training will focus upon the physical and behavioral indicators of possible substance abuse, which could lead to reasonable suspicion testing. The failure of an officer or firefighter to participate in this training shall not render the results of a reasonable suspicion test invalid or inadmissible in any disciplinary action under this policy. PROHIBITED CONDUCT

808.00 The use, possession, delivering, dispensing, manufacturing, selling or purchase of alcohol or illegal drugs as set forth in the current Collective Bargaining Agreement by members of the Fire Division is strictly prohibited.. Members may not work with positive levels of illegal drugs or alcohol as set forth the collective bargaining agreement, even if those drugs or alcohol were ingested during their off-duty hours and off City property.

808.02 All uniformed members in the Fire Division are prohibited from engaging in the following specific conduct as set forth in the current Collective Bargaining Agreement: • Reporting to work or working under the influence of alcohol and/or drugs; • Consuming alcohol at any time during the work day or the four (4) hours prior to the beginning of the work day, except that if an employee refuses overtime because he has consumed alcohol four (4) hours prior to beginning of the overtime shift that refusal will not affect the employee's place on the call-in list, nor will it be grounds for disciplinary action; • Consuming or possessing alcohol anywhere on any city premises or job sites, including City buildings, properties, vehicles and the employee's personal vehicle while engaged in city business; • Possessing, using, selling, purchasing, manufacturing, dispensing any illegal drug at any time and at any place; Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VIII Substance Abuse Policy and Procedures • Abusing any prescription drug, whether prescribed for the employee or another person. • Failing to confer with their physicians when prescribed any medications and immediately reporting to their supervisor any restrictions imposed by their physicians. USE OF PRESCRIPTION DRUGS

810.t: 810.00 A member who is using therapeutic (i.e., prescription) drugs or
p: 810.00 A member who is using therapeutic (i.e., prescription) drugs or over-the- counter medications must report the use of such medications to his/her supervisor prior to the beginning of the employee's shift if the substance could impair coordination, cause drowsiness, or could otherwise interfere in the safe performance of duties. If a member is unable to perform his duties safely because of his prescription medication, he may be required to take sick leave rather than remain on duty.

810.02 If the member is unsure as to whether a particular medication has the potential to impair job performance and thus warrants reporting, he/she must consult a physician, a pharmacist, or the product package label. In the case of prescribed substances, their use must be medically indicated and explained as such in writing by the member's prescribing physician. The member must submit written verification of such (i.e. physician's letter or prescription) to his/her supervisor for maintenance in Division records for as long as the member is required to take the medication.

810.04 When the above described medical verification is provided, a member may be permitted to continue working as long as the Division's Medical Review Physician determines that such use does not pose a threat to the safety of co-workers, the public and/or the member. Furthermore, that its use will have no adverse influence upon the member's ability to competently perform his/her job. If these safeguards cannot be ensured, however, the member may be required to take sick leave, a leave of absence, or comply with other appropriate requests made by the Fire Chief until such time as the course of medical treatment is discontinued. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VIII Substance Abuse Policy and Procedures VOLUNTARY REQUEST FOR ASSISTANCE

812.00 Members are encouraged to seek professional help, whether through the Employee Assistance Program (EAP) or from a private substance abuse professional, with any substance abuse problem. Any member who voluntarily seeks help shall not be disciplined; but, in accordance with the current Collective Bargaining Agreement, must do the following: (a) Agree to cooperate in and successfully complete appropriate treatment as determined by the substance abuse professional(s) or physician(s) involved; (b) Discontinue use of illegal drugs or misuse of alcohol, (c) Agree to authorize persons involved in counseling, diagnosing and treating the member to disclose to the Fire Chief, the Public Safety Director, the City’s attorneys, and the EAP Administrator, the member's progress, cooperation, drug and alcohol use, completion or noncompletion of counseling and treatment and any threat to property or safety perceived in connection ·with the member's continued performance of his or her job duties; (d) Complete any course of counseling or treatment prescribed, including any " after-care" group for a period of up to twelve (12) months, and (e) Agree to submit to random follow-up testing up to eight (8) times per twelve- (12) month period for the following thirty-six (36) months (i.e. the 36 months following entry into treatment).
812.02 Members who do not agree to act or who do not act in accordance with Section 812.00 of this manual shall be subject to discipline, up to and including discharge.

812.04 The member cannot return to active duty until it is determined that the member's current use of alcohol or drugs does not inhibit the individual from safely performing his/her duties or constitute a direct threat to property or safety. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VIII Substance Abuse Policy and Procedures

812.06 Treatment and rehabilitation costs arising out of a member's Voluntary Request for Assistance services shall be paid for by the member's insurance program, subject to any deductible, co-payment and policy limits under the member's insurance program.

812.08 Members will be allowed to use their accrued and earned leave (vacation, sick leave, or comp time) or to take an unpaid leave of absence for the necessary time off involved in a Voluntary Request for Assistance rehabilitation program. EMPLOYEE ASSISTANCE PROGRAM

814.t: 814.00 The City maintains an Employee Assistance Program (EAP), which
p: 814.00 The City maintains an Employee Assistance Program (EAP), which provides help to members and their family members who have alcohol, drug abuse or other personal or emotional problems. Professional counseling services are provided by a group of mental health providers. The initial services are free, and members may contact the EAP on their own without CFD permission. The Employee Assistance Program shall hold voluntary requests for assistance with drug and/or alcohol problems strictly confidential to the extent required by law and the terms of the current Collective Bargaining Agreement. Only upon written authorization by the employee may the EAP inform the Fire Chief, the Public Safety Director, and the City's attorneys, of any such request or any treatment that may be given and those city employees shall hold such information strictly confidential. All such information shall also be available to the Union Officer(s) to whom disclosure is specifically authorized if the member authorizes such disclosure in writing.

814.02 For substance abuse problems each member should voluntarily seek rehabilitative assistance through EAP, by a self-referral, before alcohol and/or drug problems negatively impact job performance or lead to a violation of the substance abuse policy.

814.04 Once Reasonable Suspicion or Random Testing has been conducted, subsequently requesting assistance through EAP on a voluntary basis cannot be used as a defense to the imposition of disciplinary action and will have no influence on the determination of the type/severity of discipline. Since referrals to EAP will not be permitted in lieu of disciplinary action, a member should understand that the member cannot avoid discipline by opting for EAP assistance once a policy infraction occurs. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VIII Substance Abuse Policy and Procedures

814.06 Correspondingly, a member can be assured that his/her decision to seek voluntary assistance through EAP prior to testing positive will not result in disciplinary action, in and of itself, provided that he/she successfully completes treatment and maintains a commitment to oneself and the CFD to remain alcohol and/or drug-free. Part of such an agreement must include periodic, follow-up drug/alcohol testing for a specified period of time, and evidence of passing the tests to ensure continued commitment (as set forth in the current Collective Bargaining Agreement).

814.08 Although the CFD strongly supports the rehabilitation of members from substance dependencies in order to return them to productive service, it contends that the strict approach described above is essential in an industry where public safety is so at issue. To adopt a more lenient approach (one whereby members can circumvent or lessen discipline following a policy violation by voluntarily entering rehabilitation) may diminish a member's incentive for making a voluntary, up-front, self-referral. For instance, a member may risk being caught under the influence of a substance if he/she reasons that employment will not be in jeopardy contingent upon willingly entering the EAP. Member perceptions of this sort are dangerous. Such a system, as appropriate and feasible as it may be in some industries, would probably be counterproductive in public safety; it may well impede safety rather than promote it. CFD philosophy should help to encourage self-referrals before alcohol and/or drug problems create hazardous conditions or events, consequently threatening an individual's employment. TYPES OF TESTS

816.t: 816.00 In accordance with the collective bargaining agreement between
p: 816.00 In accordance with the collective bargaining agreement between the City and the Union (IAFF Local 67) and pursuant to this policy, members of the Columbus Fire Division are subject to the following types of tests: • Reasonable Suspicion • Random • Return to Duty • Follow-up Testing Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VIII Substance Abuse Policy and Procedures TESTING STANDARDS

818.00 Laboratory Certification: An outside contractor to provide collection services, laboratory testing and medical review of test results shall be selected by joint agreement of the City and the Union. The laboratory performing any drug test analyses shall be certified under The Health and Human Services (HHS) federal standards.

818.02 Licenses and Certifications: Any facilities and personnel administering breathalyzer tests shall hold all necessary licenses and certificates required by law and shall be approved by the Union. If these facilities are subcontractors of the outside contractor assisting in the administration of the drug and alcohol-testing program, the Union approval of the contractor is also approval of its subcontractors. SPECIMEN COLLECTION / TESTING FOR DRUGS

820.00 Breathalyzer tests and urine specimen collections will be collected, stored and transported in a manner consistent with HHS guidelines. Records establishing the chain of custody of all specimens shall be made and maintained by the outside contractor. If the chain of custody for any sample is broken in any way, any positive test shall be invalid and may not be used for any purpose (unless the City demonstrates that the break did not affect the reliability or accuracy of the results.) Any such test shall not be counted against the number of tests to be performed annually.

820.02 Collection of urine samples shall be conducted in a manner that is consistent with HHS guidelines. Urine specimens shall be collected in private, except in the circumstances described in 49 C.F.R. section 40.25(e)(2) of the HHS guidelines. A split urine sample shall be collected in all cases of drug testing for an independent analysis in the event of a positive test result. All urine samples must be stored and preserved in a manner that conforms to HHS guidelines. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VIII Substance Abuse Policy and Procedures

820.04 On the screening test, urine specimens will be analyzed for the following drugs in the stated concentrations: Marijuana metabolites 50 ng/ml Cocaine metabolites 300 ng/ml Opiate metabolites 300 ng/ml Phencyclidine 25 ng/ml Amphetamine 1000 ng/ml Methaqualone 200 ng/ml Benzodiazepine’s 300 ng/ml Barbiturates 200 ng/ml OxyContin 100 ng/ml Ecstasy 500 ng/ml Synthetic Marijuana (K2/Spice) 20-5.0ng/ml Synthetic Cathinone’s (Bath Salts) 20 ng/ml

820.06 If the screening test is positive for one or more of the drugs listed above, a confirmation test shall be conducted, using gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (GC/MS) analysis. The level of illegal substances must meet or exceed the following guidelines for confirmation tests: Marijuana metabolites* 15 ng/ml Cocaine metabolites** 150 ng/ml Opiates: Morphine 300 ng/ml Codeine 300 ng/ml Phencyclidine 25ng/ml Amphetamines: Amphetamine 500 ng/ml Methamphetamine 500 ng/ml Methaqulone 200 ng/ml Benzodiazepines 300 ng/ml Barbiturates 200 ng/ml OxyContin 50 ng/ml Ecstasy 300 ng/ml Synthetic Marijuana (K2/Spice) 20-5.0 ng/ml Synthetic Cathinone’s (Bath Salts) 20 ng/ml * Delta 9 tetrahydrocannabinol 9 carboxylic acid **Benzoyl ecgonine

820.08 These concentration levels may be revised by the City to remain consistent with any changes in the HHS guidelines. All urine specimens shall be tested for adulterants. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VIII Substance Abuse Policy and Procedures BREATHALYZER TESTING

822.00 Alcohol tests performed under this policy shall be done with an evidential breath testing device (EBT), otherwise referred to as a Breathalyzer, which device has been approved by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA). The EBT must print out the results, the date and time of the test, a test number, and the name and serial number of the EBT. It shall also include the identification of the breath alcohol technician (BAT) conducting the test.

822.02 A breath test shall be required to determine if a person has an alcohol concentration in excess of 0.04 grams per 210 liters of breath. Any results less than 0.04 concentration shall be considered a negative test; any test at or over 0.04 concentration shall be considered a positive result requiring confirmation. Any EBT test result indicating an alcohol concentration of more than 0.04 shall be confirmed by laboratory analysis of a blood sample. The confirmation level of the blood test shall be an alcohol concentration of 0.04 grams per 100 ml. of blood. In the case of a member who refuses to submit to a blood test, the positive Breathalyzer test will stand and will be considered as a positive result. RANDOM TESTING

824.00 All uniformed employees covered by the Collective Bargaining Agreement in the Fire Division shall be subject to drug and alcohol testing at random during their workdays. Annually, there will be a number of drug and alcohol tests equal to twenty-five percent (25%) of the total number of employees. Drug and alcohol tests will be conducted reasonably throughout the year.

824.02 Members will be selected for drug and alcohol testing by the outside contractor from a list of employees provided to the vendor by the City. That list shall be updated monthly or as necessary, to include new hires and to delete those persons who have resigned, retired or otherwise been terminated from City service. Members will be selected by a City identification number, and the contractor shall not use any other identifying Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VIII Substance Abuse Policy and Procedures information in making the selections. The contractor shall select employees for random testing using scientifically valid method.

824.04 Random drug and alcohol testing shall be coordinated by the DAC in the Human Resources Department, who shall ask the outside contractor to generate a random list and coordinate the scheduling and testing with a Division representative. All testing will occur during a regularly scheduled workday for members. If member is off on sick leave, vacation leave or other leave, he/she will be excused from testing, but remain subject to random testing in the future.

824.06 Members shall be notified that they are to be tested and taken to the testing site as soon as possible thereafter. The member will be transported to and from the testing site by a supervisor, who will remain with the member until he/she is tested. After being notified of testing, members may drink water in reasonable quantities, but may not consume any substance intended to adulterate urine specimens.
824.08 In the case of random testing, transportation will be performed by SO4. REASONABLE SUSPICION TESTING

826.00 When the City has reasonable suspicion that an employee: (a) is under the influence of alcohol or is consuming or possessing alcohol in violation of the contract and this policy; or (b) is abusing prescription drugs; or (c) is possessing or using illegal drugs, or (d) a member has five (5) or more lates or absences in a calendar year, the City may require the employee to submit to drug and/or alcohol testing. Except for those instances where the reasonable suspicion is based on the possession of alcohol or illegal drugs in violation of the collective bargaining agreement, or based on five (5) or more absences, the member must exhibit physical signs. Examples of these signs are set forth in Section 826.02 below. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VIII Substance Abuse Policy and Procedures

826.02 If a supervisor has reason to believe that a member is under the influence of drugs or alcohol on the job, the supervisor may initiate reasonable suspicion testing. At least two supervisors or acting supervisors must personally observe the member and agree that the member exhibits physical signs of being under the influence of drugs and/or alcohol. These physical signs may include, but are not limited to the following: Poor physical coordination unsteady walking Hand tremors Slow reactions and clumsy movements Slurred speech Odor of marijuana or alcohol about the employee's Person Dilated or constricted pupils Glassy or bloodshot eyes Disorientation Difficulty concentrating Restlessness or nervousness Sleepiness Unusual aggressiveness or combativeness Raised voice or unusual talkativeness Possession of suspected illegal drugs Consumption of drugs or alcohol Runny nose Deterioration of personal hygiene

826.04 Supervisors may utilize form PI-11, Reasonable Suspicion Incident Flow Sheet during the decision making process. The supervisors should document their observations using Form PI-18, Reasonable Suspicion Incident Checklist and write statements documenting their observations. The supervisors should immediately contact the Drug and Alcohol Coordinator (DAC), or designee, in the Human Resources Department, through the onduty Deputy Chief or their Bureau Head. Relate this information to the DAC, who will act as a consultant to the officers. The DAC can be contacted at any time, day or night. The written statements or forms should be submitted to the DAC through the chain of command as soon as possible. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VIII Substance Abuse Policy and Procedures

826.06 If a supervisor has reasonable suspicion that a member has been abusing or misusing prescription drugs which do not fall in the listed categories in this policy, the DAC can consult with the testing facility to request a test for such prescription drugs, using the levels for screening and confirmation established by the testing laboratory in accordance with HHS guidelines.
826.08 When a member is to be tested, the requirements of Section 828.00 shall be followed REASONABLE SUSPICION INCIDENT PROCEDURE

828.00 The following personnel will be permitted to request a reasonable suspicion alcohol or drug test: 1. Any officer in the Division of Fire or 2. Any firefighter who is working in an out-of-class position.

828.02 As one of the personnel mentioned in Section 828.00, if you have a firefighter or officer under your command that you believe to be under the influence of alcohol or drugs, a second officer will be called in to confirm a reasonable suspicion. As stated in Section 826.00, a member to be tested must exhibit physical signs, or be in possession of alcohol or illegal drugs, or have five (5) or more lates or absences in a calendar year.

828.04 A second officer will be called in to confirm a reasonable suspicion. If the suspicion is confirmed, then proceed to Section 828.06. If the second officer does not believe there is reasonable cause, then the first officer may: 1. Reevaluate your suspicion and agree with the second officer. At this time, the process will be terminated. Document incident and place in file 2. You may call in a third officer (next higher officer in your chain of command). When the third officer arrives, the three officers will go over all information with regard to this incident. If two of the officers agree there is reasonable cause, then proceed to 828.06. If two of the officers Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VIII Substance Abuse Policy and Procedures do not agree there is reasonable cause, then the process will be terminated. Document incident and place in file. All information will be documented on a Reasonable Suspicion Incident Checklist (Division form PI-18), with the signatures of all officers involved.

828.06 If the decision is made to proceed with the reasonable suspicion test, then the Drug and Alcohol Coordinator (DAC) will be contacted through the on-duty Deputy Chief or Bureau Head. The DAC may offer technical assistance but the decision to test rests with the observing officers. If the member is to be tested the DAC will make arrangements for testing with the outside contractor and notify the Deputy Chief or Bureau Head of the location for testing. The DAC will notify the testing site of the specific test(s) to be performed.

828.08 The observing officers shall have the authority to order a reasonable suspicion test based on observable behavior. In such cases, the firefighter will be informed of his/her right to IAFF Local 67 representation. It is the decision of the affected firefighter whether or not to have Union representation. If he/she wishes, the member may have a Union representative with him/her throughout this process. However, the testing process will not be delayed if a Union representative is not immediately available. Unreasonable delay means twenty minutes for alcohol or two hours for drugs. The observing offices shall see that the necessary written notice setting forth the facts and inferences from such facts, which form the basis of the order to test is filled out for presentation to the member per Section 842.04. If the person under suspicion refuses to be tested or refuses to sign the Member Consent to Testing form (Division form PI-33), document this and inform them that refusal of either is considered a positive test. The person will be relieved of Duty and will be subject to disciplinary action as set forth in Sections 846.00 - 846.10 of this manual.

828.10 If the person under suspicion agrees to be tested then the Deputy Chief or Bureau Head will contact the Alarm Office and request transportation for a drug test (see section Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VIII Substance Abuse Policy and Procedures 832.00). The observing officers will remain with the member until the transportation officer has arrived. One will remain with the suspected firefighter or officer at all times.

828.12 The suspected firefighter or officer will not be permitted to leave the room, nor will they be allowed to eat or smoke. If they request something to drink, then they will be allowed no more than 12 oz. of water.
828.14 The firefighter or officer will be transported to a collection site in accordance with Section 832.00 - 832.16.

828.16 If the person being tested is transported back to their assigned station or office, the officer in charge of that firefighter or officer will request that they call someone to pick them up and drive them home. If the firefighter or officer tells the supervisor that the firefighter or officer does not have someone to pick them up and drive them home, then the officer in charge will arrange to have the firefighter or officer transported to their home. If the firefighter or officer insists on driving himself or herself home, then the officer in charge will advise them that the Columbus Police will be contacted and given the description and license number of their vehicle.

828.18 If at any time during this process, the piece of equipment that the person making the reasonable suspicion or the one suspected is assigned to, is dispatched on a run, and that vehicle cannot meet the minimum staffing requirement without them, then that piece of equipment will be called out of service. Any officer called in to confirm a suspicion will call out of service at the time they are notified of the suspicion and remain out until the suspected person has refused or has been transported to a collection site.

828.20 Any firefighter, who believes that another firefighter or officer is under the influence of alcohol or drugs, may report this to the immediate supervisor of that person. That officer will investigate and: 1. If he or she believes there is reasonable cause, then they will go back to section 828.00 and proceed from there. 2. If he or she does not believe there is a reasonable cause, they will discuss this with the firefighter that brought it to their attention. If the Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VIII Substance Abuse Policy and Procedures firefighter agrees with them, then the incident will be documented and no further action taken. 3. If he or she does not believe there is a reasonable cause, but the firefighter that brought it to their attention still believes there is a problem, then the officer will document his or her feelings and call a second officer. 4. If the second officer does not believe there is a reasonable cause, then this will be explained to the firefighter who initiated the complaint. The incident will be documented and no further action taken. If the second officer believes there is reasonable cause and the first officer does not, then refer back to Section 828.04 for a third officer's opinion and proceed from there. TIME OFF PENDING RECEIPT OF REASONABLE SUSPICION TEST RESULTS

830.t: Time Off Pending Receipt Of Test Results
p: 830.00 Except in instances of periodic follow-up, a member will not be permitted to work pending receipt of the test results. He/she will be paid any available sick time for the time off from work while "fitness for duty" is being determined. If the member passes the test, he/she will be credited back the sick days that he/she was charged while test results were pending. If the employee passes the test, has no sick time available, he/she will then be paid at his/her normal hourly rate for all hours lost. TRANSPORTATION FOR TEST

832.00 In the case of reasonable suspension testing, transportation will be performed by EMS11. Transportation for reasonable suspicion testing will follow the next steps. When there is a reason to have a firefighter or officer tested, the Deputy Chief or Bureau Head for 40-hour personnel will contact the Fire Alarm Office (FAO) and request transportation for an alcohol and drug test. The FAO will be given the location for the transportation officer to report to. At no time will the FAO be given the name of the person to be transported. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VIII Substance Abuse Policy and Procedures
832.02 The FAO will notify EMS-11 via telephone and give them the location to which to report. At no time will this information be given out over the radio.

832.04 If EMS-11 is on a run, he/she will be taken off that run and report, without delay, on a Signal X to the location that they are given. If EMS-11 feels that an EMS officer is needed on the run that he/she was taken off of, he/she will notify the FAO to replace him/her on that run with another EMS officer.

832.06 If EMS-11 is out of service, transporting someone to a collection site, and transportation is needed from another location, then the FAO will contact EMS-12, EMS-13, EMS-14, EMS-15, EMS-16, or EMS-17, whichever is closest to the station or office requesting the transportation. This will be an officer that is permanently assigned to one of these vehicles. At no time will a firefighter working out-of-class be permitted to transport someone to a collection site for reasonable suspicion testing. If none of the EMS officers are available, then a battalion chief will be used for transportation.

832.08 The transporting officer will give the FAO his/her ETA. The FAO will contact the Deputy Chief or Bureau Head, via telephone, and confirm that transportation has been arranged and give them the ETA.

832.10 The officer responsible for transporting someone to a collection site for reasonable suspicion testing will at no time be permitted to transport that person by him/herself. If staffing permits, a firefighter from the station involved in the incident will accompany the officer to the collection site. If staffing does not permit, a medic will be called out of service. If a medic is not available, or the location of the closest one might unreasonably delay the transportation, then the Engine Company at the involved station will be called out of service. If the officers initiating the reasonable suspicion test requests to go along, and staffing permits, he/she may do so and a firefighter will not be needed.
832.12 During the transportation, the officer in charge will not let the firefighter or officer out of their sight at any time until testing is completed.

832.14 When the test is completed, the supervisor shall transport the member to his home if the member is unable to make other transportation arrangements. The member should Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VIII Substance Abuse Policy and Procedures not be permitted to drive himself, and if he does, the supervisor shall notify the Columbus Police Division, giving the license plate number and a description of the vehicle.

832.16 The member shall be relieved of duty and remain off duty until the test results have been received by the Drug and Alcohol Coordinator. If the test results are negative, the member may return to work on the next regularly scheduled day, and shall be paid for any work time missed while relieved of duty. If the test results are positive, the member shall be required to agree to act in accordance with the requirements of the current Collective Bargaining Agreement. The member will remain off duty and may not return to duty until he/she has been evaluated by a substance abuse professional as defined in the HHS guidelines. The member may use vacation leave or compensatory time to cover this absence. A member may use sick leave in conformity with the current Collective Bargaining Agreement, and any applicable policies or work rules. POSITIVE DRUG OR ALCOHOL TEST

834.t: 834.00 The following will be considered to be positive tests: (a) Drug
p: 834.00 The following will be considered to be positive tests: (a) Drug tests which meet or exceed the standards set forth in the Contract; (b) Drug tests which indicate abuse of prescription drugs; (c) Alcohol tests which meet or exceed the standards set forth in the Contract; (d) Refusal to submit to a drug or alcohol test when so ordered by the proper authority; (e) Refusal to sign the "Employee Consent to Testing" form (PI-33); (f) Submitting an altered urine specimen for drug testing. PROCEDURES AFTER POSITIVE TESTS

836.00 The DAC will not notify members if the tests, i.e., reasonable suspicion, random, and follow-up, are negative. When he/she receives notice from the outside contractor that a member has a confirmed positive test, the DAC will notify the Fire Chief or his/her Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VIII Substance Abuse Policy and Procedures designee. The Fire Chief or designee will then notify the member and relieve him/her of duty. The Fire Chief or designee will make sure the member agrees to act in accordance with the requirements of the current Collective Bargaining Agreement. The DAC or Fire Chief or designee will advise the member that he/she must cooperate in an evaluation for chemical dependence and refer him/her to the Employee Assistance Program (EAP). If a member consults an outside substance abuse professional for an evaluation, he/she shall provide the DAC with a copy of the evaluation. The EAP will monitor the member's progress in treatment and confirm that the member is complying with all program requirements. The member will remain off duty until the EAP confirms he/she is ready to return and tests negative on a return to duty test. The return to duty test will also be scheduled by the DAC and all results reported to the DAC. The member will be returned to duty on his/her next regularly scheduled shift after being notified by the DAC of the test results. If the result is positive, the member will remain off duty, the DAC will notify the Fire Chief or designee, and disciplinary action will be initiated.

836.02 A member who disputes a positive result of a drug analysis may request that an analysis of the split specimen be conducted by notifying the DAC within seventy- two (72) hours of receiving a positive test result. The member may have the test performed at the laboratory of his/her choice, providing said laboratory meets HHS guidelines. The member will pay the cost of such testing prior to the actual testing.

836.04 Any refusal to submit to a drug or alcohol test will be construed as a positive test result. The member will be required to comply with all requirements (i.e., relief from duty, evaluation and treatment, return-to-duty test, follow-up tests, etc.) if this is a first positive. If the refusal is a second positive, the member shall be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination. RE-ENTRY CONTRACT

838.00 A member who has tested positive during a drug or alcohol test, or who has voluntarily entered rehabilitation without a drug or alcohol test, must enter into a Re-Entry Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VIII Substance Abuse Policy and Procedures Contract with the City and the Division of Fire before being permitted to return to work. Form PI-36, Substance Abuse Policy Conditional Employment Contract, is the Division of Fire's Re-Entry Contract which the member must sign and agree to act in accordance with.
838.02 The Re-Entry Contract must include an agreement to comply with all the terms required by of the current Collective Bargaining Agreement.

838.04 Members who do not agree to act or who do not act in accordance with the current Collective Bargaining Agreement, whichever section applies, shall be subject to discipline, up to and including discharge.
838.06 Members who refuse to enter into a Re-Entry Contract shall not be permitted to return to work and shall be subject to discipline, up to and including discharge. FOLLOW-UP TESTS
840.00 Members who are permitted to return to work must submit to follow-up testing, per the current Collective Bargaining Agreement.
840.02 The DAC and the outside contractor will determine the times and places for the followup testing. RECORDS AND DIVISION FORMS

842.00 The DAC will handle all matters related to drug and alcohol testing in the strictest confidence. The DAC will maintain all records relating to drug and alcohol testing. These records will be kept confidential and will only be released to member or a person designated by written authorization. No records of drug or alcohol testing will be maintained in the member's personnel file.
842.02 Written statements and/or forms submitted to the DAC through the chain of command shall be placed in a sealed envelope and sent to the Fire Chief.

842.04 A written notice shall be filled out for presentation to the member within twenty-four Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VIII Substance Abuse Policy and Procedures (24) hours of the time the employee is ordered to submit to reasonable suspicion testing. The written notice shall include Division form PI-18, Reasonable Suspicion Incident Checklist

842.06 Division form PI-11, Reasonable Suspicion Incident Flow Sheet, is to be utilized by an officer that has a reasonable suspicion that a uniform employee under his/her command is under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

842.08 Division form PI-18, Reasonable Suspicion Incident Checklist, is to be utilized when an incident has occurred which provides reasonable suspicion that a uniform employee is under the influence of drugs or alcohol.

842.10 Division form PI-33, Employee Consent to Testing, is to be utilized when a uniformed employee who is suspected of being under the influence of drugs or alcohol has been ordered to be tested for alcohol or drugs.

842.12 Division form PI-36, Substance Abuse Policy Conditional Employment Contract, is utilized by an employee who wishes to avoid immediate termination for a first time violation of the substance abuse policy. MONITORING OF MEMBER'S COMPLIANCE

844.00 For purposes of monitoring a member's compliance, the member will be required to sign a release of information form. This form will allow the DAC to communicate with the EAP. The EAP will refer the member to a substance abuse professional, who will establish a regimen of treatment for the member to follow while relieved of duty. Once the EAP is satisfied that the member is in full compliance with their recommendations, the EAP will contact the DAC and notify of the member's compliance and request a return-to-duty test.

844.02 If the member is required by the EAP to continue treatment after returning to work, the EAP will notify the DAC if the member fails to comply with the EAP's requirements. Failure to comply with treatment recommendations shall result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination. Revised 06/03/2016 Chapter VIII Substance Abuse Policy and Procedures DISCIPLINARY ACTION

846.00 The City will not discharge a member who tests positive a first time (whether reasonable suspicion, random, refusal to test), but may suspend such member. The length of such suspension shall be determined on a case by case basis, but shall not ordinarily exceed ten (10) calendar days unless, as set forth in the current Collective Bargaining Agreement, the employee has failed before the end of that 10 day period to provide the City with the results of an evaluation. This limitation on discipline shall not limit the City in imposing discipline up to and including termination, for gross misconduct, which may be coincident with a member's improper drug or alcohol use. If member tampers with a specimen, that test will be considered positive. Members will be terminated after a second positive drug or alcohol test, or any other drug related offenses.

846.02 In order to avoid the penalty of termination, and be subject to only a ten (10) calendar day suspension, a member who tests positive for the first time must comply with all the terms and conditions of the current Collective Bargaining Agreement.

846.04 Members who voluntarily request assistance shall not be disciplined on the first occasion if said member complies with all the terms and conditions of the current Collective Bargaining Agreement. Members who do not comply with the terms and conditions of the current Collective Bargaining Agreement, or who voluntarily request assistance a second time may be disciplined up to and including termination.
